Along the way, you will pass a reclining Buddha and caves that once sheltered monks.Watch out! Flip-flops and sandals are unsuitable. It was a bit slippery because it had rained at night. body: Climbing Pidurangala Rock was one of the most memorable experiences of my time in Sri Lanka. If you're staying near Sigiriya, this hike is absolutely worth doing especially for sunrise.I started the climb around 5:15 AM after paying the modest entrance fee (500 LKR). You pass through a small temple at the base, so remember to dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered) and remove your shoes. Once past the temple, the trail gets real.The hike is moderately challenging not too long, but the terrain shifts from a clear path to uneven stone steps and then full-on rock scrambling near the top. The final 10 minutes are a mini-adventure themselves; you’ll need both hands free to climb over big boulders, but it’s nothing too dangerous if you take your time.At the summit, you're greeted with an unobstructed panoramic view, with Sigiriya Rock rising dramatically out of the jungle. It’s honestly breathtaking. The early morning mist, the sounds of birds waking up, and the golden light hitting Sigiriya make it feel almost surreal. It was calm, not overly crowded (though people definitely arrive for sunrise), and had a peaceful energy that made the climb even more rewarding.There’s no railing, no safety barriers you’re standing on raw stone looking out over miles of forest. It's not a manicured experience like Sigiriya Fortress, but that’s part of its charm. It feels more raw, spiritual, and connected to nature.Go early for sunrise. Bring a flashlight or headlamp.Wear shoes with good grip especially for the rocky section at the top.Bring water, and maybe a light jacket if it’s chilly before dawn.Be respectful at the temple this isn’t just a tourist site; it’s sacred.Don’t rush the descent rocks can be slippery with morning dew.Overall, Pidurangala isn’t just a great alternative to Sigiriya it’s a destination in its own right. It’s cheaper, quieter, and the view is arguably better because you get to see Sigiriya itself, standing alone in the distance.
title: Worth Every Step A Peaceful Sunrise at Pidurangala Rock

body: Pidurangala Rock, located near Sigiriya, offers one of the best panoramic views in Sri Lanka—especially of the iconic Sigiriya Rock itself. body: If you're a fan of panoramic views and slightly off-the-beaten-path experiences, Pidurangala Rock is a must-do. body: Pidurangala Rock is a hidden gem in Sri Lanka that offers breathtaking views and a unique hiking experience. Overall very much doable with help and views and worth the effort.
title: Beautiful scenic views from top

body: Don't be fooled by reviews saying it was an easy 15 minute climb—if you're a couch potato like me, it's definitely no picnic! There are two stages to this climb: the first stage, which has steep, uneven steps but a definite marked pathway; and the second stage, which is climbing and hiking on an unmarked trail over rocks.We were 3 not-so-active women in our 20s-30s. We finished the first stage, and even that took some effort. Not a leisurely activity by any means! If you don't have any health issues, though, it's doable, and very rewarding. The view from the ledge after first stage is beautiful, especially in the early morning! There is also a very neat statue of the reclining Buddha. I was game to try the second stage but decided against it—sun was already up and we wanted to see Sigiriya. There is a temple at the base of the Rock, but we didn't visit as we wanted to reach Sigiriya before it got too late. All in all i found it tiring, but fun, and enjoyed my time! Might not go for a second time until i'm fit enough to take on the second stage haha
title: A fun activity but better suited to fitter folks

body: Fantastic view across the jungle to the Sigiriya Lion Rock fortress. We stayed very close at Danu’s Homestay so an 8am departure with Danu allowed us to avoid the heat and after the sunrise rush. After a challenging scramble we were lucky enough to spend 1 1/2 hours sitting enjoying the incredible views.
title: Climb Pidurangala for stunning views

body: We started the hike at about 515 and took us approx 20min-30min to get up. Pretty fit. Didn’t take any water bottles we were okay as it was still dark and not hot. The pathway was lit,we didn’t know till we got there as it was pitch black at 515 but we bought a torch anyways. The last 20M is hard you need to pull yourself up on some stuff. Kinda good to do with a friend. We took the wrong path up and my partner had to pull me up but then we realised we took the wrong rock path but it was dark. So we came down a different way. Anyways we weren’t so much interested in the sunrise it was more lion rock. You’l see where everyone sits but we choose a different spot and it was Dead quiet. As you finish the rock climb there is small pozy you can sit and it was just peaceful
title: Started walk at 515am. You snooze you lose if you don’t go early

body: The mountain is really great, and so are the views, but do you know what the best part of our trip is? The locals. They’re said to be very friendly – up to a point. We left our tuk-tuk at the base of the mountain, and when we came back down, all the fuel had been drained. The guys working at the ticket office and the man who runs the small shop right at the entrance caused us this trouble. Don’t buy anything from that guy, and think twice about leaving your vehicles there. It's outrageous. Turns out, they behave worse than animals.
title: "We gave them money, and they got us into trouble."

body: The climb is somewhat difficult, but when it is narrow, almost near the top, there should be someone to control the climbs and descents. I couldn't get up to the top because it was crowded with people coming down
title: Organization is needed

body: Magical sunset moments ❤️❤️❤️It’s was good vibe and fresh air Great views of the lion rock and the surrounding jungle.Nice place to visit
title: Pidurangala rock

body: Adventurous walk partly via stairs and partly via rock climbing. Very nice and within 30 minutes we were upstairs. Last piece the children (9 and 5 years) needed some extra help, but that is quickly found with other tourists or locals.360 degree views are spectacular and excellent for taking beautiful pictures of the Lion’s Rock. It is recommended to go early before sunrise or late afternoon before sunset. Entrance 1,000 rupees (+/- 3.25 euros) per adult, children free. Highly recommended to do.
title: Great view of Lion’s Rock

body: We visited here as Sigirya was closed due to wasps. It was a fantastic trek up but be warned it is not easy. The steps are steep and the final part is literally scaling a huge rock. If you are a shorty like me, it is a real challenge. I would advise sturdy walking shoes with good grips. Definitely worth the trip but come prepared!
title: A hard climb.

body: The ascent to sunrise is highly recommended, the path is well lit and easy to walk until a short stucco at the end. The last piece requires kick safety. Be there in time otherwise it accumulates when descending the view is very nice
title: It's worth it

body: We had read about how nice it was to climb this cliff and see Lion Rock outside of many other tourists and we went up there to see the view at sunset There were a lot of other tourists who also thought...There was a lot of crowded at the end and the ascent therefore took a total of 1 hour instead of 25 minutes.And then the sun was hidden behind clouds 😅But the view was amazing!
title: You're not alone!

body: We stayed with 2 children (6&9 years old) at sunrise on Pidurangala. The steps are easy for the children to master and also the last few meters to climb the children with little support. Walking time with the children: 45 min. Great experience! Recommended.
title: Also easily done with children and highly recommended

body: I preferred this rock to the Lion Rock, it was much quieter, more peaceful and only cost 1000LKR per person. It felt more authentic than Lion Rock.Stop at the cave temple on the way up to see the Buddha and paintings. Ladies need to cover shoulders and legs but they have a rack of scarves and sarongs which are free to borrow just to wear in the temple site. Hang them up before starting up the steps and then grab them to go back through the temple on the way back down.The walk up only takes around 20 to 30 minutes depending on your pace. The first part is on stone steps and the last stage is a scramble. When you get to a big boulder before the ridge, the easiest routes are either to the left of the boulder or underneath it.The views from the top are incredible and you can see the Lion Rock really clearly. Fantastic 360 degree views of the whole area.
title: Definitely worth a visit

body: There are basic washrooms at the base of the rock and on entering you pass through a temple therefore cover ups are required and enforced.The walk/climb uphill is of a moderate nature and anyone with a decent standard of fitness will find it a bit of an amble, even in 30° heat.Our party of 9 had varying degrees of fitness and unfortunately several of them did not complete the climb, but everyone made it to the reclining buddha.The final part of the climb was the trickiest as there were several large boulders to navigate.At the top the views were breathtaking with some very instagrammable shots of Sigiriya rock.
title: Breathtaking

body: Nice ascent of the 2nd rock or mountain in Sigiriya. As mentioned earlier, this rock fits much better in the budget than the more than 10 times more expensive adjacent Lion's Rock. With the tuktuk you are quite quickly at the entrance which is via the temple. Then you walk up in half an hour. First and canniest part via the uneven stairs, monkeys and other animals. Then the reclining Buddha and a little bit of clambering to get on top. Good to do and on top of the rock the view is amazing.Entry through the temple is 1,000 LKRClimb up for about 30 minutes. Upstairs you are an hour to watch, take pictures and watch people.
title: Beautiful view

body: We started out at 6 am, which means that we missed sunrise, however that also meant that we missed the crowds (LOTS of young people were coming down then) and we actually had the entire top to ourselves almost the whole time we were up there, and daylight, and daylight for the tuk there, and nice light and still not too hot.It is currently 1000lkr for entry.The steps are rocky, steep and uneven. It is a bit tougher than Sigiriya. Took us about 40 mins to get up (including lots of photo stops, and a couple of puffing spots).The last bit does involve “bouldering” for a short section (5 mins). But as I said, very achievable even for us, and no guide, or pushing/pulling required. Take your time, take care (you would NOT want to get injured up here)Great views of Sigiriya rock and surrounding plains. Worth it!Wear decent shoes Take care descending
title: Achievable! (overweight & 48, + 69 yo, with no help)! Worth it!

body: A must not to be missed to discover a breathtaking view of the Lion Rock at sunset but be careful the second part of the ascent from the Reclining Buddha is very very difficult because you have to climb large rocks...
title: A must-see Pidurangala!

body: Sunset seekers, look no further than Pidurangala Rock! This climb might be challenging, but trust me, the reward is absolutely worth the effort. Unlike Sigiriya's Lion Rock, Pidurangala offers a breathtaking panoramic view with Sigiriya itself as the centerpiece. Imagine watching the fiery hues of sunset paint the sky while this majestic rock formation stands tall in front of you. For adventurers on a budget, the entrance fee is just 1,000 LKR for tourists (free for locals), making it an even more attractive option. Don't miss out on this unforgettable experience!
title: Sunsets and Budget-Friendly Views

body: Definitely the rock to climb first when around Sigiriya. Wake up early, do the climb for the sunrise, take wonderful pictures of Sigiriya rock, enjoy the view then go down and move to climb Sigiriya itself.Climbing Pidurangala is easy, there are some stairs , a very small element of scrambling , but nothing that an average person would not be able to do. It will take you 45 minutes to climb it from the start of the trekking path at good pacing. The view to Sigiriya breath-taking! Going early for the sunrise gives enough time to go down and then move to Sigiriya before the heath and the massive tourist crowds.
title: Climb for the sunrise, look at Sigiriya and then climb Sigiriya

body: Omg…. Climbing up to the Pidurangala rock was a great cardio exercise… I lost the count of the stairs but is worth every heartbeat…. The views when you reach the top is something else… must do!
title: Pidurangala rock climbing

body: Two stars for my own experience not the place itself!I had read a lot about this and Lions Rock to make the decision which to choose. I knew this was tougher physically but felt confident enough to try. We waited until it was light but still 6am. It isn’t easy for the most part but doable with moderate fitness until you reach the part near the top. For me this was just not possible. The rocks at this part are steep and flat with nothing to grab onto and I did not have the body strength to pull myself up high enough to hold on to anything. I seemed to be the only one stuck here, but then learned that many people had been pulled or pushed up for the sunrise so unlucky that we had no one to help but I still think I would have struggled. I was also wondering how I would get back down again if I somehow managed to go further.It is not for anyone with limited strength and whilst mine were ok, the knees take a good battering on the way down. Disappointed not to get there and I’m sure they could add in a few pullys or handles to hold on to that would mean it is accessible to more people.I would say try it! But be prepared to accept it if you can’t manage the last 50 feet or so. There is still a nice view.
title: The last part proved too difficult for me!

body: Superb place to see the sunset over the whole region and on the lion rock. The climb can be done in 30 minutes at a good pace. The first part consists of irregular stairs, the second part from the reclining Buddha requires climbing rocks (very short part, barely 5-10min).On the other hand, if you want to arrive at the summit at the right time, plan widely: in fact, the short but more strenuous part of the climb was completely blocked by visitors: some were not in the condition to tackle this section but forced themselves when even if they weren't really moving forward, or didn't have appropriate shoes, so it was risky. Also some went down and the crossing is difficult or even impossible at several levels. We were stopped for more than 20 minutes despite the short distance that separated us from the summit and were able to access the plateau just before sunset.
title: Great view

body: The Pidurangala rock is spectacular. You have to invest some energy to get up there but it is definetly worth it. Try to catch the sunset or sunrise. The last part is very tricky. You have to be very careful when you come down to not miss a step. It could be dangerous
title: Spectacular view

body: Tickets now mandatory, about a thousand. Sunrise ascent has a good chance of being grey and foggy unless you come in summer, but sunset hitting Sigiriya from here must be pretty amazing if you head up in the late afternoon.
title: Morning is hit or miss; tickets mandatory

body: The Piduralanga offers a magnificent view of Lion RockThe ascent is not very easy on the last part and there are a lot of people at the top at sunset but the view is incredible!Access is payable for a small fee
title: Superb walk with incredible view

body: It was very nice to see the sunrise on the mountain. There is a beautiful view of Sigiriya. The cost is much lower than the nearby mountain. The climb at the end has elements of rock climbing, but everyone can climb. I recommend visiting to watch the sunrise, but the sunset is just as good there...
title: A good alternative to the nearby mountain

body: A decent climb up a lot of steps initially followed by some bouldering at the end made the views all the more rewarding when we reached the top for sunrise. A local chap was guiding people how to scramble over the final rocks to reach the top, which then allowed everyone to copy. There was even a couple of wild dogs and monkeys at the top! Beautiful views of Lion Rock. Well worth the effort of getting up at 4.45am to meet the tuktuk driver who drove us there - felt safer with him because he’d have known what to do if we came across an elephant which apparently is not unheard of at this time of day🐘
title: Fantastic views of Lion Rock and the surrounding vista

body: Amazing view. Best place to visit in sigiriya area in sri lanka. Greate place to hikers. Low budget place. Good for photograph
title: Amazing view

body: Not an easy climb with irregular steps and, at the end, quite complicated passage to reach the summit. Once at the top, great, incredible view of the region and, opposite the lion rock
title: To have

body: We paid 1,000LKR at the entrance and went up without a guide. It’s up irregular rock steps until the last 50m or so when it becomes a tough bouldering challenge. We made it to the top and were rewarded by an incredible 360deg vista. Even if you decide not to go to the very top, it’s still worth going as far as the reclining Buddha. Not as commercial or busy as climbing Sigaria Rock and the benefit of seeing that landmark at eye level. Wear good walking shoes and clothes suitable for bouldering. We loved it.
title: A spectacular viewpoint for those that don’t mind a short but adventurous hike

body: We visited on an overcast day to climb the rock, having read that this rock gave a good view over the main Lion’s Rock that people flock to Sigiriya to climb.The rock was a lot cheaper to climb that it’s neighbour and offered good views from the top. The majority of the climb was ok, mainly with stone steps, however the last 10m (5 mins or so) were very much “off roading” with a moment where you need to pull yourself up an almost sheer sheet of rock with a rope.Safe to say I bailed out on seeing this and left my partner to climb to the summit where the view of the other rock was. He reported that this last bit of the climb was treacherous and that people were being helped by guides and other more experienced climbers to get up and down.As it was slightly damp when we climbed this made it a bit more of a tricky ascent, and we were offered a guide by the ticket office, which we think wouldn’t have been needed, until the last section mentioned above. But people were helping each other out here as it seemed dangerous - regardless of if you had a guide or not. The views from the platform I stopped at (just prior to the peak with the laying Buddha) were nice, but you couldn’t see the Lion’s Rock.Ladies need to have knees covered as there is a temple on the way up! You can borrow a cover from the ticket office for your ascent. Overall, it was an ok experience, but not as easy as made out online and in the Lonely Planet, but by all accounts did give a great view of Lion’s Rock from the top.
title: Ok climb, with very steep scary section at the end!

body: Nice walk up with uneven stairs, at the end som tecnical climbing. Beautiful view to Lions Rock and the surroundings. Can be at little crowded mornings an afternoons.
title: Nice walk and beatiful views

body: The short hike that goes up to the top of the rock is not very long, but a little arduous at the end. You have to climb a rock a little to access the plateau and finally have this magnificent view of Lion Rock. We loved the view at the top, we could have stayed there for hours. We made it for sunset.
title: For the view

body: The day we reached SriLanka, we headed for Sigiriya where we trekked the Pidurangala rock to get the sunset view. It took ~45 min to climb the rock, including adequate rests. There are stone made steps throughout the journey. Some bhramhi inscriptions, inclined Buddha statue can be seen on the way. It used to be very early settlement of Buddhist monks. Last 50 -100 m climbing was very challenging with no defined steps and almost vertical/ steep climbing on rocks ! But the view from the top was worth taking the risk. Recommend to use sport shoes, light wear and bagpack. Carry water. Try to return as soon as the Sun set, since it becomes difficult to walk in low light condition.
title: Thrilling adventure for best sunset view

body: A day trip from Kandalama. If you have visited Sigiriya this is an excellent alternative. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes, so that you can scramble over the rocks. No disabled access.
title: Fantastic views from rock summit

body: Capture love atop Pidurangala Rock. Majestic views, eternal moments. Elevate your romance with stunning backdrops
title: very good experience

body: The view of Lions Rock and the panoramic view are unbelievably beautiful! Good shoes are recommended, as there is a bit of scrambling at the end and it is slippery in places. It is all doable and so worth it! And the 1000 LRS are well invested :D
title: definitely do it - the Pidurangala is incredibly beautiful!

body: It is an excursion that is not for everyone because the route is not only uphill, but at times dangerous because it is more of a climb. We arrived at the top at sunset and enjoyed a breathtaking view and Sigirya Rock which we would visit the following morning. If we had not climbed here, we would not have been able to see the most famous rock from this perspective. I therefore recommend both excursions
title: Not to be missed

body: You have to pay to climb but only $3( the other rock is $30) in a way this one is better as you have the view of Sigiriya Lion Rock, but there is no ruins at the top. Bit of a climb mainly stairs .. the top part is a bit of a scramble. I wouldn’t advise in the rain We went at sunset there is a great view . Our driver / guide came up with us and I was glad he did . If you are a bit unfit you can do it .. just take slowly and stop to rest . It’s worth it
title: Fantastic view

body: In the dark, with a headlamp, we go up to the lookout point.After about 30 minutes of climbing, which gets a bit tricky towards the end, we reach the top. The awakening jungle and the sunrise quickly wash away the effort.You have a wonderful view of Lions Rock and the surrounding land.
title: Pure goosebumps

body: Amazing view point. You can see all around the sigiriya rock and amazing view. Pidurangala rock is calm place.
title: Amazing place

body: A must to do for a beautiful view of the lion rock!Quick and relatively simple climb (except the last part).Much fewer tourists than on lion rock and that is appreciable.We did it with a 14 month old baby without any worries!
title: A must do for a beautiful view of lion rock!

body: Personally, I liked the Pidurangala rocks better than the Lion Rock. The entrance fee is LKR 1000, which is less than €3, compared to the Lion Rock, which costs around €30. The view is also much nicer, as you can see from the Lion Rock, among other places. The climb requires a certain level of fitness and the last few meters even require some skill or climbing ability. Make sure you wear good shoes and avoid climbing when it's raining, as the rocks are slippery! The panoramic view is breathtaking.
title: Better Pidurangala Rock than Lion Rock

body: The climb is long and tiring, but the view that greets you when you finally reach the top is worth everything. The summit is very windy, be sure to carry appropriate clothing. Sports shoes must be worn
title: Difficult roads lead to amazing places

body: Really nice.Took about 20 minutes to climb to the top.The last 5 minutes was challenging, it was differently not for everyone. But normal people, not necessarily in good shape or anything, can do it. Being water, there were no vendors anywhere.You can borrow a shari to wrap around you, they are hanging before the temple to use.
title: Really nice

body: A walk in the low light of dawn, and enjoy from this smoky place, after climbing a few stairs, the end is a little complicated but short, it is worth it,,,
title: very good......

body: Well worth the 1000lkr spent :-) no crowds and spectacular view. It was a bit of a climb at the end, but not too challenging. We reached the top in approximately 20 minutes.
title: Spectacular view

body: I had the privilege of hiking to the top of Pidurangala Rock, and I can confidently say that it was an unforgettable experience.The hike itself is both exhilarating and rewarding.. As you ascend, you'll be surrounded by the lush, vibrant greenery of Sri Lanka's countryside.Pidurangala Rock has an elevation of approximately 340 meters (1,115 feet) above sea level. As for the number of steps, there are around 500 steep and uneven steps that you'll need to climb to reach the summit. You start by passing through a temple, so need to remove shoes and cover knees and shoulders for 1st 100m. The entrance fees much lower than other places. It’s about $2.75 per person. The place has no toilet facilities.Early morning or late afternoon climb is advisable. 5.30am to 7pm it’s open for visitors. But, if you don’t have drive, try to climb down before too dark because tuk tuk is very expensive at night.The climb can be challenging, but the breathtaking views from the top make it well worth the effort. Upon reaching the summit, I was met with a panoramic view that left me in awe. The 360-degree vista includes the iconic Sigiriya Rock in the foreground and stretches out to the distant horizon, showcasing the beauty of the region. Watching the sunrise or sunset from Pidurangala Rock is a memory that will stay with you forever.Whether you're an avid hiker or simply seeking a nature-filled adventure, Pidurangala Rock is an absolute must-visit. Don't miss the opportunity to explore this gem in Sri Lanka; it's a true testament to the wonders of Mother Nature.Happy hiking!
title: "A Spectacular Hike amidst Lush Greenery"

body: You have to go there for the sunrise, it's magnificent!The climb is physical but it's worth it.
title: Very beautiful view

body: Nice rock.great experience,I went with Russia, USA,Italy, UK, Czech Republic, Denmark, Ukraine guests.all guests were happy to climb this rock.further,guests can visit sun rise,sun set and and lion rock.i start to climb this rock since 2018.
title: Best place in Sri Lanka 🇱🇰

body: Pidurangala Rock is an incredible 360-degree viewpoint located opposite the world-famous Sigiriya Lion Rock. Hiking to the top is possible for both of these rocks, but hiking at dawn to the top of Pidurangala Rock is a real adventure. You get a good view of Lion's Rock itself. There is a small fee and the climb is not easy!
title: Pidurangala Rock

body: Really tiring especially because rather than a road there is a path with randomly placed stonesThe last stretch is also dangerous because you have to climbBut when you get to the top you forget everythingWonderful showSigiriya at sunset gives you chillsWorth a trip
title: Marvelous

body: When in Sigiriya definitely go up Pidurangala Rock. The entrance fee is a couple hundred of rupees and thus nothing compared to Lions Rock. Be prepared for quite the climb over some rocks and don’t just wear sandals. You will pass a temple to be prepared to cover up and remove shoes in that part. We went to see the sunrise which was beautiful with a spectacular view of Lions rock, but very windy. Walking down it was already pretty dark. To get back to our guest house by tuktuk was expensive because the Tuk drivers know that you cannot walk home in the dark because of the elephants so they will charge high rates…
title: Spectacular view of Lions rock and sunrise

body: Just wonderful! We decided to go upRock early in the morning to admire the sunrise and the effort mixed with the heat was ABSOLUTELY worth it. I don't understand those who say to do this climb and avoid Lion Rock: trust me, do both (I did Sunrise here and Sunset on Lion Rock). The climb is more difficult than the Sigirya rock because it is a path and often, especially in the final part you will have to climb a rock: complicated but absolutely doable. The 360 degree view is breathtaking. If you come to Sri Lanka Pidurangola and Lion Rock are a must do.
title: Wonderful!

body: The views were amazing. Pleasant climb as mostly it is through the shade of trees. Some parts the climb is quite steep and needs extremely caution
title: Great views of Sigiri Rock

body: Hike to Pidurangala is a must. We went for the sunrise and it was soooo beautiful. The hike is not long but quite adventurous. The entry fee is LRK1000 per person. You can see Sigiriya temple and other monuments from the top.
title: Hike for the sunrise!

body: Super great view. You should definitely be good on foot and it is recommended to start walking in the morning around 05:15 am to see the great sunrise and escape the heat. The last part is certainly not easy but with a pair of good sneakers and reasonably ok fitness more than good to master. In my opinion no more strenuous than any other rock (e.g. Sigiria Rock or Little Adams Peak).I would climb it again and again.
title: Great sunrise!

body: An amazing sunrise hike! You start by passing through a temple, so you need to remove shoes and cover knees/shoulders for first 100m or so. It is dark, so follow the lights up the mountain - if you deviate from the lights you will get lost! There are stairs 3/4 of the way up, past the Pidurangala cave temple with a huge reclining Buddha statue. For the final 1/4, it is quite a clamber up and over rocks - you don’t need to be a seasoned climber but do need decent agility to get up to the top. Definitely bring trainers for once you’re past the temple. At the top, there are great views of Sigiriya rock and lots of space to sit and watch the sunrise.
title: Beautiful sunrise hike

body: Pidurangala is a gem! The lesser known rock formation offers panoramic views with Sigiriya Rock in the foreground and serene atmosphere make it an unforgettable experience. The experience leaves an indelible mark, reminding us of the immense beauty that exists in the world and the significance of preserving such treasures. I was a bit worried seeing reviews about the hike’s difficulty, but if you’re in good shape, you’ll do just fine (I don’t exercise and had feet injury and was able to do it). The hike might be challenging, but the reward is worth it.
title: Absolute gem

body: The hike is easy but need strength to climb the top at the end. The view is amazing. Worth to visit sunrise or sunset.
title: Amazing overlooking view Sigiriya from Pidurangala.

body: An awesome climb for the best view of Sigiriya. Please note that you will have to remove your shoes at the white picketed gate as you reach a Buddhist temple. They also provide scarfs to cover yourself if you’re in a singlet - there is somewhere to go them off to before you make your ascent. This is a challenging climb for someone with not great knees/joints as the steps are unevenly placed/thickness. Near the top there is a beautiful Buddha on its side inset into the rock. The final scramble is not for the faint hearted you will need upper body strength to pull yourself up. The pay off is THAT view as you crawl through the final opening. It’s spectacular. On a clear afternoon it’s priceless. You can see why lion rock is the 8th wonder if the world.It was extremely windy at the top.
title: You gotta work for it but it’s worth it

body: Climbing the Pidurangala rock will treat you with a stunning view of the Sigiriya citadel.Early morning or late afternoon climbing is advisable to avoid scorching sun.However, this climbing is not suitable for old people, pregnant mothers or kids as climbing to the top will be through rocks and no proper staircase. Good pair of sneakers will be more beneficial.There is a temple on the way to the top of Pidurangala and therefore climbers are required to cover there legs and arms properly.If wearing a short, there are some clothing available at the entrance until you pass the temple.
title: Best view of the Sigiriya Rock

body: I highly recommend Pidurangala rock over Lion's rock. The hike is easy in the beginning with steps and is slightly uphill with beautiful high trees all around, until you reach a short rocky spot towards the end where you need to kind of climb some rocks for less than 5 minutes to get to the top. The view is mind blowing at sunset as you can spot the Lion's rock and see the Pidurangala round rock as well. The hike down is easier than up and the trail is lit with lamps. You can also do it at sunrise but it's as magical at sunset and less hot to walk down at night than in the morning. More reviews @myra.recommends
title: Mind blowing sunset views

body: We climbed the rock for sunrise and it was an amazing experience. The kids are 5 and 7 and they were able to do it with the help of a guide. We got one from the hotel so I highly recommend that as some parts are a little difficult to get through.All in all a super experience!
title: One of the best views !

body: This is an absolute must do if you’re in Sigiriya. Full 360 degrees of the area and one hell of a sunset.I’d recommend getting up there a good 45 mins or so before the actual sunset, just to make sure you get a good spot and don’t get caught in the queue. It takes about half hour or so to get up and is a little tricky to scale the rocks in the last 5 mins… but if you’re semi-fit and agile you’ll be fine.
title: Even better than Lion Rock

body: Beautiful views from the top of the city and the Sigiriya rock. Truly a wonder in Sri Lanka. The climb itself was exciting and adventurous. Definitely something unique in the nation.
title: Unique

body: We went to watch the sunrise and it was a good decision:) It was a bit cloudy at the time, but still a great view of the neighboring Lion Rock. It is wise to take a tuk tuk to the starting point if you want to see the sunrise, as there is a chance of encountering a wild elephant in the morning. It took us 15 minutes to walk from the starting point to the top. The entrance fee is much lower than for the Lion Rock - 1000 rupees and the crowd is not that big either.
title: Amazing view!

body: Climb the rock to see the rock lion about 30 min to climb. This is relatively easy except the last 100 meters you have to climb. Avoid flip-flops or shoe not close because bcp slip. We went there at 16:30 to see the sunset and it was fantastic a dazzling 360 view overlooking the jungle. In short, you have to go to understand. However the return after sunset is done in the night some lights are installed there to light but unfortunately not enough take lamb or flash of your phones. We pay 2000 RS so 5.50€ for two. You cross a temple watch out for the woman no shorts or strapless dress otherwise no worry it lends you fabrics to cover you time to cross a temple. I loved it.
title: Exceptional

body: Easily accessible. Modest dress required to pass by the Buddhist temple. Stunning views from the top which requires a bit of a scrable but achievable by most.
title: Great half day trip

body: I’ve gone on many hikes in different places around the world, but this has been the most challenging one that I’ve done. The reward is the vast, panoramic views atop the mountain. The part of the hike till the cave temple is not that difficult, but beyond it is pretty tricky as one has to climb rocks and boulders, through some narrow paths. At one point, we had to wait for about 15 minutes to move up, as people were coming down and the narrow pathway allows one way traffic only. Everyone was helping each other which was great- and the only reason I was able to make it up, and enjoy the amazing views at sunset.
title: Amazing views!

body: Super view for sun rice. But need wakeup 4:30am but it is big worth our trip you cant miss it. Enjoy srilanka
title: Amazing

body: Pidurangala rock s 200 meters / 660 feet hight .this rock s very popular trail for hiking & walking .. me & my friend has climbed & we complete hike in 45 min - 1 hrs time .. this s moderately challenging route .. last 15 min in hike bit challenging .. because need to climb .. through the giant rocks .. finally we reach top of the rock .. you can see the amazing view of sigiriya rock .. if you climb in evening.. you can see the beautiful sun dawn as well ..

body: I got picked up at by tuk tuk at about 5am from Sigiriya town to hike the rock for sunrise. It requires some clambering but is easy enough. The view is magical and our driver came up with us and took pictures... great pictures.
title: Come for sunrise. It is just wonderful.

body: We climbed to the top which gives a magnificent view of Lion's Rock and the surrounding landscape. Overall, the climb is quite easy, the end of the climb requires a little more dexterity.Getting to the top, we were surprised to see poor dogs extremely thin. If we had known of their presence, we would have brought food to give to them. So if you go, think of them.
title: Beautiful view of Lion's Rock

body: Easy access to parking. Locals helps with parking and protect your vehicle from monkeys. Please give them some money. Little difficult walking trail, seems less well maintained. It is a dream come true when you got to the top. Beautiful panoramic view. Sigiriya rock !! Very good pick nick location. You can spend some time up on the rock. Get there early in the morning.
title: Rock views

body: Climbing to the top is wonderful, the views spectacular. It was a bit scaring climbing the 1200 stairs but made it despite a sticky hot sunny day.
title: Brilliant experience

body: This steep hill near sigiriya is not as popular as it's neighbour Sigiriya fort.The hill is very steep to climb, the path is strewn with boulders and there are no handrail or steps.The entry fee of SLR 500 is rather steep.The place has no toilet facilities available.When it gets dark, there are no lights to assist the tourists to safely climb down the uneven path.Having said that, once you are able to reach the top, literally on your hands and knees, the sunset is beautiful with the majestic Sigiriya fort visible to the south.We can also see a partly damaged reclining Lord Buddha statue almost half way to the top.The top of the hill is bereft of any structure or a Buddha vihara.It is suggested that the hapless tourists may be spared the trouble of wearing uncomfortable clothes just to pass a new Buddha vihara located near the ticket office.Instead, the management of the Vihara can consider putting up a screen before the door/pinnacle. Given an option, one can always choose to climb the Sigiriya fort for its varied attractions.Wear comfortable clothes and put on your climbing shoes before attempting to climb the hill.Brush up your rock climbing skills also.You need to be not only young at heart but also have a young body to climb this rather difficult hill.Not recommended unless you have already visited Sigiriya fort and are physically very fit.
title: Pidurangala - Difficult terrain - No facilities - Beautiful sunset.

body: So, everything that you need to do when you come to Sri Lanka - it's called Bhathiya! And enjoy your vacation )
title: Great and funny trip!

body: This is definitely a rock that needs to be climbed if you want to get the best view of the Sigiriya rock!
title: Best place to hike and get a view of Sigiriya.

body: We can highly recommend climbing the Pidurangala Rock after having climbed Lion's Rock. From the summit there's a phenomenal view of the area and Lion's Rock. The trail to the summit is relatively easy, but consider hiring a guide for the trip. If you do ask for Sunil who gave us a wonderful experience on the climb. body: Me and my brother started with pidurangala, around 9am. It was a really easy but nice climb, especially the last part is really fun. We climbed the rock in 25 minutes. The view is breathtaking, even without a sunrise/sunset. It’s definitely worth it!!
title: Breathtaking view and fun climb

body: Nice place..amazing every one have to visit this place...evening is best time to visit because of the sun set..nice view wonderful
title: Wonderful place ,

body: Our driver encouraged us to do Pidurangula Rock for sunset instead of Sigirya and in my opinion it's the one bad recommendation he gave us. Yes it's 1/10th the price, but it's about 10 times more difficult. It was so hard that I actually gave up halfway!! For context I am not super fit, but I am in my early 30s and have never abandoned a climb up to any landmark before. In 30+ degree temperatures and 95% humidity, it was punishing. I saw people struggling and actually crying! The steps are uneven, crumbling and frankly dangerous. The only picture my fiance wanted from the whole trip was from the top of this rock so he soldiered on, but at 6'3 even he really struggled getting up the rocks near the end. Tourists have to help push and pull each other up. The pictures he showed me from the top didn't even look that good anyway!
title: Warning: Very difficult climb

body: Very beautiful and breathtaking view of Sigiriya. Better choice than Sigiriya. 1000 rupees for foreigner. you can skip Sigiriya Rock but you shouldn't miss this one.
title: Better than Sigiriya Rock

body: This hike is not for the faint hearted. The path from the temple at ground level up to the cave temple is rough with huge steps, crumbling step and a degraded path. Beyond the upper temple, you need to scale rocks following painted arrows. But the view is rewarding.

body: This is a must visit place if you are traveling to Sigiriya rock fortress. body: Very early start but worth it for the views!You need to have a certain level of fitness to get to the top, but we made it in time and day there watching the sun rise.Still smiling and can't believe we did it.Wonderful memories

body: The view from the top during sunrise is the most beautiful thing we have ever seen. We hiked to the top of the rock at 4 in the morning to see the sunrise and we were not disappointed. Beforehand we were not sure what to expect, as we could read a lot of different things about the difficulty online. But it was not difficult at all as there were steps most of the way. Some of them are steep, so if you are not in shape it will be difficult, but if you are just normally fit and wear good shoes and a headlamp if you are hiking in the dark, it's very doable. You have to climb three or four boulders in the end, but we were very pleasantly surprised as we have done hikes in Sri Lanka that were much more challenging and much longer. It only took us 20 minutes to get to the top. We also walked to the top of Sigiriya Rock, but we actually preferred this and it is MUCH cheaper!

body: Pidurangala Rock is only a 20-minute walk from Sigiriya Rock and costs about $3 to enter. The view from the top of the rock is more impressive than the more famous and popular Sri Lankan hill. The rock offers a chance to explore a more natural setting, visit cave temples, see what was once the largest brick reclining Buddha in the world, and experience history without the crowds. It could be the best $3 you have ever spent, and only takes about 2 hours to complete.You’ll have to scramble up and over boulders after passing the stairs for few hundred steps from the entrance. It’s a short trip, but much more challenging than the previous section or any place at Sigiriya Rock. Make sure you have suitable shoes for this section and a headlight if you’re planning to climb it before sunrise or after sunset. It's a short but difficult climb, but it's a long way to reach the top of the rock.

body: Pidurangala was one of the many stops our on tour of Sri Lanka and we had no idea what to expect! Not too hard though - the dogs and monkeys were running around up there no problem! Definitely worth a visit.

body: We visited at sunset and the view is spectacular. A must visit and if you only have time to visit one of the two rocks this would be my choice. Only 500 LKR, compared to the $30 rate for Sigiriya Lion Rock.The last section of the climb up is a short scramble, but manageable.

body: An entrance fee of LKR1,000 for foreigners to enter to this place. Before climbing up the rock, there is a Buddhist Temple at the foot of the climb. No shoes are allowed and appropriate dressing is required. The Buddhist temple was built since 5th century by King Kashyapa who killed his father (King Dhatusena) who fled to Sirigiya to avoid retaliation from his half brother, Mugalan. The built of the temple was meant for meditation purpose for the monks. Interesting graffiti within the temple with local worshippers and ritual can be seen within the temple. Two parts to climb up Pidurangala Rock. First part is pretty straight forward with proper stair case till reaching the Reclining Buddha statue at the cave. Pretty impressive authentic statue of the Reclining Buddha. Second part is after the Reclining Buddha where is more tricky with unclear path as one has to manoeuvre between boulders to reach to the top. Avoid going alone as it is possible to get lost or asking other travellers who are on the way back from the top, since there are some misleading paths. Precautions is required as it can be risky upon falling from the boulders. Upon reaching the top, the 360 degree panoramic view is well worth it especially overlooking Sirigiya Rock. Some travellers are here for sunrise or sunset watching. Our suggestion is to do Pidurangala first then proceed to Sirigiya since the later has more details to see in terms of the ruins of the palace on top, plus it is easier to do Sirigiya with proper staircase. Winds on top of the rock can be quite strong and nice to sit/ line down to relax. Total climb takes 30-45 mins to reach the top depends on individual fitness. Definitely a “No” for anyone who has phobia for heights and faint-hearted. One may need to use own discretion whether to climb to the top as we saw a couple in their 50’s gave up climbing the 2nd part of the climb, whereas a 85 years old man managed to reach to the top.
title: Panoramic overlooking Sirigiya Rock

And the last part of about 10 minutes consists of climbing on rocks with your hands and feet. Then you have a nice view of the lion rock. Sunset is beautiful to see. There are enough tuktuk to take you back to the village. Otherwise it is a walk of approximately 2.5 - 3 km.

body: We enjoyed an amazing sunset on top of Pidurangala rock. The way to climb up is not very difficult but if you are not prepared enough, it takes you more time to climb it.

We heard so many conflicting accounts of time that it takes and I think the people in front of you play the biggest factor. We read all sorts of timings; 20 mins to 2 hours for the hike. We asked our homestay to book Tuk tuks for 5 am and the timing works out perfect. Leaving the ticket booth at 5:30am in high season it took us about 30-40 mins.We enjoyed the hike, took some pics and then returned to our homestay for a breakfast and nap. If you have the time then enjoy Sigariya but I don't know if its worth the hype. There are so many other beautiful and fun activities in Sri Lanka to do.

body: We'll worth a trip up Pidurangala to see sunset. Easy walk except where it gets a little dodgy on the final ascent where you have to pull yourself up some boulders. body: It's a very good plan, access to the top is a bit complicated and you need proper shoes, but the view is worth it. body: 20 to 30 minutes walking towards top of the rock. And you will have great view of the Sigiriya Lion Rock.

body: If you have to hike one of the rocks then make it this one. The crowds are negligible and the views you get of Sigiriya are incredible. One of the few times where the view really does live up to the hype. It’s also only about a 20 minute hike up to the top - small scramble at the end. body: The view from the top is absolutely amazing, on a clear day you can see the mountains that boarder Sigiriya and you have a beautiful view of Sigiriya rock itself! The climb to the top is rather tricky, it starts with a short walk through a temple (make sure you have your shoulders and knees covered, if not you can rent a sarong) followed by a few uneven cobble stone steps. Next, you have to climb over boulders. It is quite dangerous and whist we were clambering, someone fell and grazed their head, arms and leg. We also made the mistake of going up just before sunset and on a Poya day - making it extra busy. There was a large crush with an every man for themselves scenario making it even more dangerous. It was the same scenario on the way down. Pidurangala costs 500LKR (2.80USD) per person in comparison to Sigiriya Rock which costs 5,450LKR (30USD) per person. I would definitely recommend because the view was incredible and the price is so low however I wouldn’t recommend taking young children or climbing if you’re unable to clamber over boulders

title: Excellent

body: Our trip designer (see Travel with Rana in Sri Lanka) recommended this adventure instead of climbing to Sigiriya Rock because the entrance ticket to Sigiriya Rock is 25 $ and to Pidurangala Rock it was only 350 Rs and it will be less crowded and we will get also a benefit "the best view of Sigiriya Rock... He climbed with us and we could enjoy the amazing view from the top, meditate and relax there. Do not worry to climb with children as well ;-) (it took only around 70 - 80 min to climb on the top but we took photos on the way). We were very thankful for this trip to our trip designer.
title: Amazing view of Sigiriya Rock

body: If you need to see the beauty of Rock Sigiriya...you must climb Rock Pidurangala. Please climb during the early morning or evening
title: The Best View Of Rock Sigiriya

body: its a 30 mins hike to the to of the rock. its better if you go in the morning so that you get to see the sun rise from the top of the rock. amazing 360 view. definitely this should be in your bucket list.
title: Well worth hike to the top

body: We climbed Pidurangala Rock on the advise of our driver with Indigo travel, he suggested coming here instead of Sigiriya Rock because he felt it was a better climb, it would be less crowded, less expensive and that yo also get the view of Sigiriya. He was definitely right and we were not left disappointed. The views from the top were amazing and the climb required some effort but more than manageable with moderate fitness. It took us about an hour in total and definitely bring water which can be bought at the shop at the bottom of the climb. You do have to take off your shoes and cover up for the temple part which is right at the start but can put them back on before going up.
title: Driver Recommended

body: It's can be difficult but I feel any able bodied person can do this, maybe just a slower pace if needed. Super fun climbing over boulders not just step after step
title: A MUST. Surprised its not more popular

body: We climbed Pidurangala and Sigiriya and the former is by far the better. The walk is relatively easy (despite the last little boulder scramble) and there is a lot of space at the summit to find a spot and watch a sunrise or sunset in relative tranquility.
title: The little sibling is sometimes better

body: Superb adventure. After the stature, climbing become difficult and when it is crowded, you find it extremely difficult to go up or down. something should be done. Otherwise it is more adventures than of Sigiriya though it has no such vivid history.
title: Better than Sigiriya

body: A bit of climb and a short part of the way bouldering, but the views 100% worth it. not only you can see all the Sigiriya and surroundings, but also the best view to Lion Rock!
title: Great view on all Sigiriya surroundings!

body: | The Short |This is the best way to see Sigiriya rock. The entrance is 500 rupees per person. There is parking for your vehicle just outside the main entrance.| The Long |Easily accessible by TukTuk or car Pidurangala rock is the best way to see Sigiriya rock. It is approximately 5km outside the nearby town. There are also public buses that pass the nearest junction and is approximately a 2km walk to the main entrance from here.The main entrance is easy to locate. Walk in towards the temple and the ticket office is the right. Tickets cost 500 rupees per person. The path is easy to follow but consists of multiple steps which can become slippery as they as narrown in places. However it is lit by lights if you choose to do sunrise or sunset. You will walk through a temple and it is respectful to have shoulders and knees covered for both men and women. The last part of track (after the laying down buddha) does consist of climbing over rocks and can be challenging. When you finally reach the last section head under the big rock rather than up the left or right side for an easier route to get on the rock.We went up at 7.15am and there were multiple people coming down and by 7.30am it was really quite. If you are not fussed about sunrise I would head for this sort of time.If you want to see Sigiriya rock rather than climb it this is one of the best options in the area and well worth the climb.
title: Best View Of Sigiriya Rock. Go At 7am To Avoid Tourists

body: I did this after Lions rock and it is much better. Why?More natural stairs and climbs.Less tourists.Much less pricy.Better view.And its realy easy to climb.
title: Cool one. And no buts...

body: Try to be at 9am at the temple and wear solid shoes. Enjoy the rocks you have to climb and you will gain a spectacular experience in the morning sun. I felt in love with this place.
title: Short walk to an awesome 360-view

body: We were deciding whether go on Sirigiya rock or whether try this one and I guess we decided right. The view was hilarious! Not only you have amazing view on Sirigiya rock, the surroundings is spectacular as well! I think it’s the most beautiful view on Sri Lanka so far! And we’ve been on Little adams peak and Horton plains!Lot of people warn you about the last part of the climb and I must say, that its not that bad as it seems. And I can be concerned about climbing! It takes about 30 min to get to the top. We went in the afternoon and the sun was down a bit, but still very hot! So prepare light clothes. You will get very sweaty!Also keep in mind, that firstly you have to go through temple, where you have to take your shoes off and have shoulders and knees covered. But they can borrow you a scarf, so don’t worry.The last part is challenging, but nothing impossible. Just wear a proper shoes. It can get slippy.The entrance is 500 rs. It is kind of difference comparing to the Sirigiya rock. And I guess the view is better.
title: Totally worth it!

body: We went for sunrise and it was amazingly beautiful! We didnt climb the Sigiriya rock but that was our choice.
title: Nice view!

body: Located adjacent to Sigiriya, Pidurangala provides the best viewing point of Sigiriya as its top is slightly lower. Once at the top platform, it gives a panoramic view of the surrounding area and thus it's also popular as a spot to watch the sunrise. Hike to the top of the rock takes about 20 to 30 minutes. Once you pass the Pidurangala Sigiri Rajamaha Viharaya (පිදුරංගල සීගිරි රජමහා විහාරය), you will be at the base of some steep stairs that leads to the Pidurangala Temple almost at the top of the rock. From this point to the top, it's a 5 to 10 minutes trekking with some bouldering. Its certainly no too dangerous, but could be challenging to some.
title: Amazing View

body: Very beautiful, cheap and less crowded than sigiriya! Walkin to the top is enjoyable! View and sunset unforgetable!
title: Nature!

body: This is a nice hike offering great views from the top. It can get crowded and hot so avoid noon or early afternoon
title: Nice hike great views

body: its a whole new experience .. sunrise was breathtaking , relaz on top of this rock ... cool misty environment makes it out of the world , never get tired of looking in to the horizon
title: Best Sun Rise

body: We visited pidurangala the same day we visited sigirya. I was already knackered from waking up at 7 am to get there early and from climbing the gazzilion stairs at Sigirya. Having said that climbing Pidurangala is 100% the most fun activity my wife and I did during our trip to Sri Lanka. It costs 500 rupees per person to enter ($2) compared to $20 or $30 at Sigirya.It's a steep climb and gets pretty hard at the second half but everyone can do it. I saw people with babies doing it with one hand and old people with sticks getting pushed up the hill. Apart from the fun way up you get 360 views of Sigirya, Dambulla and the nearby parks. The views are definitely better than Sigirya as you get to view Sigirya from a mountain of similar height (just 1 meter shorter)I left with major aches in my legs but I can't stop thinking about that day . I would do it again on a heartbeat.
title: The climb of your life

body: We set off 5am in a tuk tuk. We were advised against the walk as early morning & late night there is the chance of encountering wild elephants. It cost 500LKR each for entry. You start with steep uneven steps till you get to the budha statue from whence the steps fade away and its a more adventurous climb. The climb itself is slightly challenging but once at the top it really is stunning. Views were amazing and watching the sunrise was so peaceful and stunning. Definitely a must.
title: Small climb for mammoth views

body: This short walk was great. We started at about 10am and the crowds were minimal on the way up! Took us 45 minutes at a leisurely pace. The last 10 minutes weren’t bad at all. People of all ages were able to do it, with many people helping along the way if needed. From the top of the rock, we could see Sigiriya rock and the line going up the stairs was visible too - a very long line. Would recommend this climb over sigiriya. Only 500 rupees pp and a 1.5 hour round trip including a long stop at the top!
title: Great short climb!

body: We started walking to the beginning of the Pidurangala climb around 4pm from the Centre of Sigiriya town (really just a Main Street and not much more!) aiming to reach the top by sunset. A Tuktuk driver stopped as he was passing us and offered a ride for 150LKR and once we saw how much further it was we were grateful, it’s about a 4km walk to the beginning of the track/temple entrance!You start the climb by passing through a temple area so shoes and hats must come off for the first section, scarves are provided for females to cover shoulders for the temple section too, if you don’t have your own. Entry to this climb is 500LKR per person, we didn’t have to pay for our 3 and 5 year olds. A bargain compared to the 5000LKR for Sigiriya Rock but don’t expect the same kind of historical area you find at the base and on top of Sig Rock. This is really just a beautiful climb to a beautiful viewpoint. No frills.The climb itself was irregular stairs for the majority of it, our 5 year old daughter had a great time and handled the climb without problem. I carried the 3 year-old in a hiking backpack. Near the summit it changes from stairs to rock scrambling, around, under, over with a few challenging traverses but nothing that can’t be done with a helping hand from strangers coming and going in both directions. There were a couple of pinch points where we had to wait for people coming down and vice versa. The final approach to the summit was the busiest point with two way traffic being funneled through two big rocks and was the most challenging part of the entire climb but that was mainly because of the hiking backpack and headroom clearance. Totally worth it all for the view back to Sig Rock as the sun was still setting, had time for a few pics, a wander around and got back to the bottom just as it was getting dark. I would suggest aiming to leave the summit about 20 mins before actual sunset time as the climb down is on the shadow side of the rock and because of the tree cover it gets very dark very quickly. In all, I found this a much more satisfying climb than going up Sig Rock because it was a bit more adventurous and fewer tourists owing to its slightly more challenging nature.
title: Excellent rock to climb

body: Really great hiking : steps at the beginning followed by some climbing where you need to use your hands.It’s not really tiring as this is quite a short walk.Our kids (6 and 9) managed to do this hiking even if they needed some help in a few passages.The view on the top is splendid ! It’s worth it.We went there at 9 am and it was not too crowded at that time. However when we came down, there were groups going up. We were happy not to be stuck in this crowd.
title: A really enjoyable climbing !

body: Pidurangala rock was a must-do for us! Pidurangala Rock is adjacent to Sigiriya Rock and it is the best viewing spot of Sigiriya Rock as their height above sea level is about the same. Pidurangala is a popular spot for sunset and sunrise as you can enjoy 360-degree views of not only the Sigiriya Rock but also the valleys, lakes and surrounding mountains. We are rather owls than larks so we opted to go there for sunset and we did not regret it. It was a more natural ascent, way less crowded and more peaceful and the view and light on top was just amazing.
title: Popular spot for sunset

body: The scramble up all the rocks is well worth it. You need to be fit and not over weight as there are some small areas you need to climb through
title: Well worth it

body: We had walked up Sigiriya in the morning ( fantastic experience even though the rain was torrential) and decided that it would be best viewed from Pidurangala.It is a significantly steeper / harder climb than Sigiriya ( uneven / higher steps etc- far more natural surface) . The last 5 minutes were explained as a scramble - I would definitely call it climbing. We scrambled our way over and through the rock gaps and were wowed by reaching the summit.A number of people didnt get to reach the summit. Climbing down was a bit precarious in places ( not helped by the rain)A really worthwhile climb and definitely recomended. Note you have to walk past a temple on the way up so women need to be covered accordingly , for that part of the walk
title: Well worth the scramble to the top

body: We did the sunrise hike to the top and enjoyed the speed of the walk (less than a km) and slight challenge. Definitely wear trainers and have a torch if you set off in the dark. Sadly, it was cloudy so we didn’t see the sun but it was still beautiful. I would recommend doing this at sunrise and Sigiriya itself at sunset. Also, if it has been raining it would be very slippery in parts.
title: Great hike

body: The trek starts with inclined steps but later turns into a challenging terrain. Once at the top, great views of the Lion Rock and 360 degree view of the tropical jungles, lakes, mountains and farmlands. A must visit. Try to be on top before 10 am. When i was climbing down at about 12 noon, there was a bit of human traffic jam of people coming up.
title: Take the Trek for Mesmerizing Views

body: Stunning walk. Very clearly labeled. But you do need to be physically able, there are so small rambles over rocks.The view is stunning
title: Sunrise walk

body: The best time to go is for sunrise. Locals recommend to leave at 5am. Not only is the sunrise beautiful to watch, but the weather is also the best during this time--can rain later in the day. Need to wear good shoes --no sandals-- as it's a bit challenging near the top. It's about 30-45 min hike up, depending on how fast you hike. Bring a headlamp if you start early as it will be dark. You'll have a fantastic view of Lion's Rock once at the top. Site costs 500 rupee to enter. We took a tuk tuk to the base area, but some walk, it's about a 30 min walk from the center.
title: Beautiful sunrise view

body: In my opinion, better than Sigiriya Rock. The whole thing is about 20mins, at the 2nd part I used barefoot as it was better grip than my shoes. Go there with not a too heavy backpack; and maybe leave before it gets dark! Once up there it is really a wonderful experience. Some parts you are just alone, and it is great.
title: One of the best climbs of my 1-week trip in Sri Lanka

body: Absolutely fantastic view, including of sigiriya rock. The climb is very much do able for non climbers: 90 percent of the climb is easy, the last 10 percent is a bit more challenging but still fine. Its not so crowded/full up there
title: Fantastic view

body: Very good daytrip option from Kandy, but also ok to do for 2 days together with other sights. Nice view from here to Sigiriya Rock. Take eniught water and wear proper shoes!
title: Great attraction

body: Go in the evening and do bring a light if you are trekking down after 6:30 pm . It was so dark that I had difficulty seeing the track . Locals were climbing up then and we had to wait to get down. The sun set was amazing and we had a serene time at the summit admiring Lion’ s Rock .
title: Sunset at the Rock

body: Best sunset ever!! If you visit Sigyria you must visit Pidutangala, doesn't matter if on sunrise or sunset, the landscape is amazing!!

Not as easy as Dugouts but definitely worth the view. Most of the way up it's bit rock stairs but at the very end you will have to do a bit of rock climbing but nothing dangerous.It's an absolutely amazing view and as its untouched it's pretty spectacular. Take a picnic up with you for lunch and spend a few hours up on top of the world
title: Well worth the climb

body: The climb itself is not difficult however it does get challenging at the end clambering over boulders. Well worth the effort though as the views are spectacular!
title: Challenging climb but worth the effort

body: Make sure to bring sporty shoes, the view is worth the sweating while hiking to the top. There are some wild dogs around but if you leave them alone, they will leave you alone as well :)
title: Nice experience

body: Vary natural ancient cave temple. It is a challenging climb but the views of top is amazing weather was nice best time climbing is morning.
title: Adventure tour

body: amazing view of sigiriya and tall buddha status sunrise so beautiful nature view point best in sigiriya
title: beutiful for sunrise

body: Even though the climb is pretty difficult the view from Pidurangala is amazing. Had a great experience of a pretty good hike. The scenery is beyond beautiful for me.
title: Superb view. Worth the climb!!!

body: Better than Lions rock, better view, way less people, a true hike raher than artificial stairs and 500rp instead of > 5000rp. End part is a bit of a scramble, especially for the unfit
title: Hike up Pidurangala

body: Located just 15 mins from sigiriya rock. We climbed d sigiriya rock in d morning,rested for a few hours and then climbed Pidurangala at around 3pm. I would suggest please don’t delay more than 3pm to climb up,so that u can come down by 5.30 ,bcoz it gets really dark after 5.30 while coming down. And the descent gets a little risky in darkness.Theres a small temple at the bottom of Pidurangala rock. Make sure ur shoulders and knees are covered. Ull have to walk a few steps without footwear. Please make sure to wear proper shoes,its a tricky climb. The first half is easy with steps to climb. After u pass d sleeping buddha,there’s no steps,only rock climbing. Its a little adventure of its own. After a stressful rock climbing,u reach d top and ur blown by the view. It makes d last half hour of climbing worth every second. U can see d sigiriya rock from here. Spend an hour or two easily here. Just click pics. Find a spot to sit n enjoy d view. Dont miss d sunset. Its beautiful. As soon as d sun sets start ur descent. Else it gets dark too quickly. Highly recommended. Just bcoz its not too popular,dont miss it!
title: Beautiful views from d top

body: The walk to the top here is quite difficult. I would suggest it takes a fair while of time so plan ahead. We departed early morning to reach the summit before sunrise. What a decision it was! The sunrise here was perfect, especially overlooking huge areas of lush green and mountain ranges in the distance. You can also see lion rock across the views standing alone and tall above the rest.It is worth going up here for another view point of lion rock, and one that others may nit want to do because of the journey. Trust me it is worth it though
title: Great views but tough walk

body: You want to the see sunrise better you visit early in the morning. It was picturque. You wear a fully covered clothes since the path to rock is lay through a Buddhist temple it joyful to climb all rocks and risky.
title: nice view in sigiriya lion rock and fantastic view pidurangala rock

body: We went to Pidurangala early in the morning to watch sun rise and got heaps of photographs. It was picturesque. You better wear a fully covered clothes since the path to rock is lay through a Buddhist temple. It was joyful to climb all those rocks plus little risky.
title: What a view

body: We woke up before 5am to see this stunning sunrise. The trail to the peak is one of the easiest I've done with the most stunning reward. It is no wonder the hermit Buddhist monks chose this place to pray and meditate all day. You can just sit there, close your eyes, feel the wind and watch the lush forest.There are monkeys and animals along the trail. Watch your belongings and make sure your bags are closed at all times especially when bringing food along so monkeys cannot snatch them.Best to wear confortable clothes and shoes fit for hiking.
title: Great morning hike with an amazing view

body: To go to the top of the rock you have to go through a temple at the beginning. If you are wearing a short pants, have to cover your knees. Fortunately they do have some clothes (wraps) you could use for FREE. Also to pass that 50 meters you have to remove your shoes. Once you pass that temple area you could wear your shoes and remove the wraps and continue your hike. When you come back after the hike follow the same procedure and leave their wraps. Enjoy.
title: Few advises

body: Have to climb lot of steps. In the beginning it is not difficult but towards the end there is kind of a difficult climb. Specially if you have kids with you. We climbed with my 4 year old and 7 year old. So it was bit hard with them. The rock on the top is slightly slanted. Therefor have to take care of the kids running about. You can see a wonderful view around the area from the top.
title: Breathtaking view

body: More adventurous as it is "not discovered" yet.Only a few people, adventurous hike through jungle and a more difficult climbing part at the end.Lots of fun for all (2 kids 11 and 14ys)
title: Almost better than Lions Rock

body: It's simple as this. Be at the start of the climb by at least 4.30 - 5.00 AM. The views, colors and the overall vibe created during the sunrise (or even the sunset) is amazing. Make sure you don'd miss this. You shouldn't waste a single sunrise/sunset when you travel in Sri Lanka anyway. Hike up is going to be somewhat difficult but nothing too serious. Make sure you have enough time to stop along the way as you would have plenty of reasons to do so (monkeys, temples, ruins, scenic lookouts, etc). Whatever you do make sure you are on top of the rock before the sunrise. Have time to find yourself a good spot to rest, relax and soak it all in. I spent at least 2 hours up there and took enough water and bites to keep me busy.
title: Alternative Experience - More Adventurous

body: A historical place which runs back to the era of King Kasyapa in Sigiriya. The best view for Sigiriya Rock and an amazing view point for sun rise with so much scenic beauty. It is not difficult to climb until you reach to the place before the summit. Not recommended for old people who are weak but the steady ones could face the challenge!There is a buddha statue with historical value on the way to the summit. It is said King Kasyapa moved monks living around Sigiriya to a new monastery on Pidurangala Rock.
title: Quite adventurous and a beautiful place

body: This is a ancient Buddhist temple which was constructed on a massive rock. There is a hike wich later part is bit difficult and dangerous. But after that nice scenery in front of you. Don't climb mid day as it's hot. Try to see sunrise or sunset. Around 3 hours require. You must climb here, if you around.
title: Hidden jem

body: Much better choice going to Pidurangala Rock, the entrance fee is much cheaper and you get to see the beautiful and unique Sigiriya rock as part of the scenery! A great climb, challenging but not too hard, highly recommend.
title: Better Than Sigiriya Rock

body: No words needed. It’s just totally perfect place with the perfect view. Better than Lion’s rock - its more fun to climb up there.
title: Beautiful place

body: A very interesting site with an ancient Buddhist temple. Nice that sarongs are provided for covering up for tourists. The walk is steep and precarious in places with very little in the way of handrails and disappointingly the very top has no support whatsoever and is extremely precarious. Shame that the Sri Lankan tourist board are not switched onto this but still charge for entrance. So if you are expecting to see the promises view of the Lions Rock opposite, be warned that you risk your life doing so, whatever your fitness level!
title: Limited accessibility

body: Very beautiful hike. Yes, towards the end it is hard to hike. Few people turn back because they couldn't do it. Beautiful view of the lion rock. Very peaceful.
title: Pidurangala Rock hike

body: This is a lesser know attraction, but offering views just as impressive (if not better) than the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. This has the advantage of being a lot cheaper and far less crowded. This place offers a very beautiful view of the rock fortress.The flip side is that it is a relatively difficult climb, even more so when the sun is up. A couple of people i spoke to also mentioned having seen snakes but we thankfully didnt encounter any. I would suggest going here early in the morning (preferably without children), wearing good shoes and carrying plenty of water.Some people recommend missing the sigiriya rock fortress and doing only pidurangala (partly because of the high entrance fees at sigiriya) but i myself would recommend doing both.
title: Good alternative to the Sigiriya Rock Fortress

body: There is a bit of a climb towards the top which was a little scary, and needed a bit of strength, however once I was up there it was just so beautiful and exhilarating that I am so pleased I made it. What a view.
title: Terrifying! But amazing

body: This was our favourite activity in Sri Lanka! A must do activity if you are up for a hike.The path is easy to follow, very cheap to get in. The steps and stairs are the beginning are good but the final section is more difficult, definitely more like climbing. The views are 100% with it - absolutely breathtaking. A lot less people too than lion rock.
title: Better then the lion rock

body: This is the smaller rock with Sigiryia Rock close by. We found the climb to the top mostly straight forward with much of the walk step climbing. However once you reach the Buddha, the path reverts to clambering over rocks. If you are not fit and willing to stretch up over rocks then maybe stop at the Buddha. However getting to the top is very rewarding. The views are amazing especially looking back to Sigiryia Rock. It was nice to spend time enjoying the quiet surroundings and the views over the valleys.Tough it out and enjoy the rewards! A great walk!
title: Scramble to the end!

body: It is a moderate hike of 30-45 minutes. It is quite steep but there are steps till the last part. Most difficult part is the last part; it is like rock climbing. This is a must visit place when you are in Sigiriya area. Here you have the best view of Sigiriya. You can get best Instagram pictures at the sunrise & sunset.
title: Best Instagram picture with the Lion Rock

body: Hiking this huge rock was a bit challenging but the breath taking view was amazing!We took lots of pictures by our Guide Aswar and thank you Kingfisher Tours Sri Lanka for taking us here and arranging all our Tour in Sri Lanka!We are really thankful for them because we will miss these wonderful if we are alone
title: Fabulous

body: This was amazing. We were unprepared, in that we didn’t have head lamps but used our iPhones for light as we climbed in the pre dawn darkness. I would have preferred a head lamp as hands are required due to there not being an actual track. No matter what, it was worth it.It’s not too difficult or treacherous, but if you are climbing for the first time in the dark I recommend a guide (we had a driver guide who climbed with us and we still got a little lost).We came straight down and then moved on to Sigiriyia Rock which was fantastic as well - great to do both early in the day.
title: A hike for sunrise

body: Usually not in the plans for tourists, but really worth a visit! It's not as expensive as the main Unesco sites and it has less people. The way up can be tiring but done slowly, and the perfect cenario makes up for all that!
title: A place not to miss

body: Better to climb this rock than the liin rock .... cheaper! The way to climb is under the tree in the shade and less tourists! The view is wonderful ! Do it !
title: Superb

body: short hike to the top. it’s mostly stairs and not too challenging, some minor climbing in the end. the view is definitely definitely worth it!
title: great view - go there for sunrise

body: If you have time and the energy then the climb is very worthwhile. Having climbed Lion Rock the day before it was tempting to relax and give this climb a miss. I am so glad we didn’t. The views of Lion Rock and the surrounding countryside are spectacular. It is a steady climb but can be achieved by anyone with a reasonable level of fitness. Avoid the middle of the day and wear shoes not flip flops as the last section does require you to clamber up, over and onto rocks where a good grip with your feet is required. The other positive is that it is far cheaper than Lion Rock to enter. (500 rupees in Oct. 2019. At the start you walk through a temple area so are required to cover legs and shoulders. Don’t worry as Sarongs are provided. Carry your shoes and put them on at the far side of the temple. Afterwards have a swim and enjoy the view of Lion Rock if you are staying at the Sigiriya Hotel (and then a beer or vice versa).
title: Pidurangala Rock

body: Climbed this rock early in the morning and I was not disappointed. The sunrise was beautiful and the view of the Sigiriya rock majestic.Foreigners are charged an entrance fee and locals go free. At least it is much less than than the money grabbing Sigiriya rock management.
title: Worth the Climb - Foreigners are charged Rs. 500 and Locals are not changed

body: Another must do in Sigiriya! There is a short (about 15-20 min) but very steep walk up some rugged stairs to make your way to the top of this hill. After clambering over some boulders, you are rewarded with a view over lion rock and the surrounding land!
