Definitely worth while, just beware that the first hundred meters of the hike is through a temple so remove your shoes and either wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees or use a sarong to cover up!
title: A short but steep climb

body: Hi, Its located Dambulla Srilanka and closed to Sigiriya Rock. 149 Km far from Colombo airport and take 3-4 hours direct driving. Real mountain hike for this visit with the eco & nature. Little bit hot and dry activity but very interesting. Memorable photos can take this place including adventure. All facilities near their and wild elephants can be see in sometimes. Don't miss to visit the Pidurangala on your Dambulla traveling.Thanks.
title: Pidurangala Rock - Dambulla

body: A fantastic view for a fraction of the price compared to Sigaria rock. The view was just as spectacular and easier to climb. There are some parts where there is no path and you have to climb but it is so worth it.
title: Great view

body: We did this at sunrise as a cheaper alternative to Sigriya Rock and it was brilliant. We were given cover ups as we were in shorts however we did not have to pay extra for this.There are steps up most of the way and it is a little hard but takes around 20 minutes to reach the top. Sunrise was beautiful and you get a great view of Sigriya Rock also.
title: Beautiful views

body: The view at the top is worth the climb. It is a little bit tricky at the end because of rock formation and missing ladders etc. Therefore it is not recommended with small kids. The view and landscape is amazing.
title: Stunning climb and amazing view

body: We were so excited to climb the Pidurangala rock but was denied entry just because we were wearing headscarves for religious reason. I never thought to google on that because I’ve been to huge and small Buddhist temples in Japan, Thailand, Vietnam and Cambodia and was never denied entry. I guess it’s just in Sri Lanka?
title: Woke up early for nothing

body: Much better than the Lion Rock and the 360 degrees views are bomb! Better to come early to make it before sunrise as the crowds start coming around 8. The hike itself is not difficult, just the last part with big rocks and no clear path, so wear appropriate shoes.
title: Fantastic

body: This rock is very beautiful.And from the rock all the city can be seenEven the main rock is visible. It gets shorter and easier.For ticket cost was about three dollars and 20 min hike to the top, Go there at sunrise or sunset and you will be amazed.
title: Wonderful hike

body: We climbed pidurangala the day after climbing Sigiriya - we loved both but actually enjoyed the fact that pidurangala is less commercial and still has the stunning views!! The climb becomes a bit more rocky at the top so a warning that it may be difficult for some but we thoroughly enjoyed it.
title: Stunning view and fun to climb

body: A must if you are visiting Habarana Sri Lanka. We climbed pidurangala end August. The terrain is rocky natural. No artificial structures. It is fully worth the effort. Once on top. The views are breath taking. With Seegiriya in the back drop. And very strong cool breez blowing accross. It is a photographers dream. It can get hot around 10.30am to 1.30pm. Wear a hat and sun cream. The climb would be easier with trekking/hiking shoes .Although it is not a difficult climb.
title: SIMPLY BEAUTIFUL

body: Climb at the latter part was bit messy but its worthier enough with great views on the top. Easily accessible to the bottom of the rock by car with google maps. Better to climb it in the morning as when its noon, its bit hotter than you expect.
title: Awsome Views of Sigiriya

body: We didnt think climbing up this huge massive rock will give a best view but recommending by our Tour Company we started hiking this rock,Make sure you take water bottles and good shoes where it is a bit slippery upwards.The view from the Top was really amazing we really enjoyed the wonderful snaps and thanks to Aswar (Our Tour Guide) for suggesting us this place
title: Hike to Paradise

body: This is a place of historical importance. At the entrance you will find the temple and a devala. You have to climb up and may be difficult if you have any disability for climbing steps.Also as this a religious place of worship need to cover your self similar to other temples.
title: one of the important palces to worship

body: The rock can be reached after a short hike and climb. The reward is a magnificent view on Sigiriya Rock. Still I'd consider it a great add-on not an alternative to climbing Sigiriya Rock itself , because what Pidurangala cannot give you is the view on the city walls /structures and on the historic site. We went on Sigiriya Rock in the early morning, and Pidurangala in the late afternoon. A great combination - my best day in Sri Lanka!
title: Great Place, terrific view

body: Very adventurous ancient place with some slippery areas. Beware if you travel with children. You have to be very careful at the end of the edge with heavy wind blowing.
title: One of the best place with adventure

body: We went here rather than Lion Rock because price of tickets(30 USD for Lion Rock, and 3 USD for PIdurangala) and we can see the view of whole Lion Rock . Before you climb Pidurangala, there are a temple where you can buy the ticket and you should take off shoes and cover your shoulders and feet ( if you wear sleeveless clothes and short pants). After that temple you can wear you shoes and don't need to cover your shoulders and feet. Climbing on the top of Pidurangala, it takes aroud 10- 20 mins. On the top of Pidurangala, there are strong wind. If you are afrid of cold, don't forget to bring your coat. On the way of climbing, there are some Buddha made by bricks and in the cave of mountain wall.In addtion, there are a lot of trees on the way, so you can enjoy your trip under the shade. Unlike climbing the Lion Rock, there are few trees and it's much hotter. On the top, you can enjoy the view of whole Sigiriya and Lion Rock. It's awosome and the nature. 我們來了Pidurangala，而不是獅獅子岩，因為門票價格（獅子岩需要30美元，PIdurangala卻只需 3美元），但是這裡我們可以看到整個獅子岩的景色。在你爬Pidurangala之前有一間寺廟，你可以在這買票，但是到寺廟時需脫掉鞋子並遮住你的肩膀和腳（如果你穿無袖衣服和短褲）。在那個寺廟後，可以穿鞋，不需要遮住肩膀和腳。攀登Pidurangala山頂，需要10-20分鐘。在Pidurangala的山頂風還滿強的。如果你怕冷的話，要記得帶外套。在攀登的路上，有一些用磚砌成的佛像和山壁的洞穴。此外，路上還有很多樹木，所以你可以在樹蔭下享受旅行。與攀登獅子山不同，樹很少，而且更熱。在頂部，您可以欣賞整個錫吉里亞和獅子山的景色。這是一個很棒的和自然的。
title: 從Pidurangala欣賞Lion Rock風景

body: This place is amazing, It is a 30 mins hike, some areas we had to climb rocks, it is not than hard but it is pretty fun, We enter thought a Buddhist temple area, so shoulders, knees should be covered, they provide a silk if you need it. The small temple is nice, with a very strong energy and beautiful painting in the rock wall. On the hiking there are many trees, kind of jungle, another reclining Buddha is close to the top, after the final and more challenging climb, there is an amazing view waiting for you, the impressive Lion rock is there. After you can go a little bit more up and have 360 view, very impressive. People go there for Sunrise and Sunset I bet would be stunning. Note: drones are not allowed.
title: Incredible energy and view

body: Climbed Pidurangala Rock in the morning.Took about 30-40 minutes and was a reasonable climb up. Had to clamber over a few rocks and boulders near the top. There is always someone there to give a helping hand . A great 360 view of the area as well as Sigariya Rock. Well worth the climb
title: Fantastic Views

body: This is a wonderful rock to climb in Sigiriya area. Amazing view and it is just opposite of the famous "Sigiriya" lion's rock, Definitely worth climbing.
title: amazing view....

body: We visitted for sunrise which was well worth the hike. Be warned the hike is a little bit difficult if you want to do under half an hour. There are some challenging parts but to see for sunrise is worth it!
title: Beautiful sunrise

body: Firstly the area around and route to the top is clean and free of litter. The last climb to the top of the rock is difficult as there is no proper route, once at the top the views are spectacular and you can see the sigiriya lions rock. The price difference is great therefore I suggest you try this rock first. It also has good history
title: Well worth the effort

body: This rock is amazing, it’s a hard climb if you are not young and fit, but we did it!! You climb through caves and over boulders and lots of steps but well worth it when you see the views from the top
title: Amazing and a must do

body: When you visit Sigiriya rock citadel do not miss to hike Pidurangala Rock as well. Why because it would be another amazing hiking throughout the forest root. It is a very beautiful and large scale rock top which you can visit surround pictorial view nicely. The whole hiking and get downtime would be 2 hours and it will vary with the crowd.
title: Two birds in one stone - Sigiriya Rock n' Pidurangala Rock

body: I arrived in Sigiriya planning to climb both Pidurangala and Sigiriya but in the end I only did Pidurangala because the views were amazing. I’m travelling on a pretty tight budget so the cost for Sigiriya ($50 Australian) was very steep. I went in the afternoon hoping for sunset but I wouldn’t recommend waiting until it got dark to leave as it is a serious scramble up boulders for the last little bit and without light it would be pretty easy to hurt an ankle. The Buddha is impressive too. There was also a small swarm of bats on the way down but they didn’t attack us, just interesting!
title: A scramble up the rocks but so worth it! And so cheap!

body: Our tuktuk driver dropped us off just before the entrance. Just after buying the ticket at the office, you pass a temple which is worth paying a visit. The stairs next to it will lead you to the top of the rock. The last part can be a little challenging as you will have to climb your way up to the top. When you arrive at the top you have a breathtaking view of the Lion's Rock and the surrounding.
title: Easy climb and a breath taking view for sunrise

body: We had an amazing experience from the top of the rock and had a picturesque view of sigiriya. A must visit place when touring sri lanka. Worth paying rs500/= for the ticket.
title: Amazing view from the top!!

body: Excellent view of Sigiriya rock. Exciting hike up to the summit. If you stay at "Back of Beyond - Pidurangala" you can walk to Pidurangala rock (5 minutes away).
title: Great view

body: large rock face at the top to walk around. Awesome little place. Best time to hike would be around 4.30pm.he entrance ticket is 500/= (LKR) (2.5 $) for foriegners. Climb to start rock is through ancient buddhist temple. you get 360 degree view. It's a nice experience compared to Lion's rock.
title: Lovely afternoon.....

body: Climb up is bit hard and may struggle at the last part. Literally the views were amazing and worth the hike. Entrance ticket was just 500 rupees.
title: worth the hike to see the amazing views

body: Climbing to the top is not easy. Comfortable clothing and footwear are essential. Also physical fitness. You have to enter to the route through a Buddhist temple. So make sure you cover yourself to pass a religious place. After passing the temple it doesn't matter. It'll take 1.5 hrs to climb if less crowded. Otherwise up to even 2.5 hrs. At some places it's very difficult to climb up. But everyone helps each other so you'll somehow get through it. Eventhough the hike is challenging you will feel it's absolutely worth when you climb up. The view is amazing and cant express it in words.. you should see it by yourself.Excellent place to take nice pics. Specially the view of Sigiriya. At the top it's very windy. So be careful on your hats.You can see ancient Buddha statues also on the way to the top. Getting down is very much easier than climbing. Take plenty of water as you wont find water through the entire journey. If you are a person who loves adventure and nature this place should be in your bucket list when you visit Sri Lanka.
title: Amazing view

body: As sigriya rock can get very busy, and is quite expensive, I really recommend climbing pidurangala as an alternative or as well! There is an impressive buddha statue towards the top after a fairly straight forward climb. If you want to get to the tip of it though be prepared to scramble your way up through some rocks and do a bit of climbing! Make sure you wear trainers but the stunning view is worth it!
title: Great alternative to sigiriya rock

body: Lovely afternoon climbing!Wonderful views of Sigiriya, less crowded, plus a great sunset seen at the top!At the beginning of the hike you will need to cover shoulders and knees.Only a small scramble at the top, lots of steps! Throughly enjoyable 🤗
title: Hiking fun!

body: You head up from a temple and climb over 1400 steps to the top. It is hot work with a scramble at the top before you see Sigiriya in front of you. You will pass a sleeping Buddha on the way up which is very old. Please make the effort for the view
title: Worth the effort to see Sigiriya

body: Pidurangala rock is right in front of the Sigiriya rock ( Lion rock ). The hike could be a bit challenging, but the view makes up for it. You can get a great view of the sigiriya rock and the surroundings from the top of pidurangala.The best time to hike is early morning or evening, because you can get a fantastic view of the sunset or sunrise. But i personally recommend to go in the morning, because it is usually less crowded and easy to climb int the mornings.Pidurangala hike usually takes around 45mins to 1 hour climb, might be even less if you are a quick climber.So if you visit Sri Lanka, don't forget to hike Pidurangala..!!!
title: Great hike, great view !!

body: I‘m not going to lie. The way up is exhausting but the view will make up for it. Since the entrance is at a temple you have to make sure to cover shoulders and knees while crossing the premises. But you can just take a scarf they provide at the entrance. After this the hard part starts and you are climbing towards the rock. Once you arrive you have a beautiful view over Sigiriya and Lion‘s Rock. Also it’s much cheaper than Lions Rock which is $30 for foreigners compared to 500 Rupies at Pidurangala.
title: No pain no gain!

body: It's much more of a natural and isolate feel up here. Open and large rock face at the top to walk around. Feels a bit other-worldly. A lot less crowded than Lion Rock and a fraction of the cost. After being to both within 24 hours, it was not even close. It's a much better view of Lion Rock from here than it is of the landscape below from Lion Rock. Cheaper. More space. Less people. Better photos. More natural. No brainer.
title: Better Than Sigiriya

body: Short but intense hike but what a rewarding view. Totally worth it but also worth going to Sigiriya of your budget permits.
title: Amazing

body: Fantastic way to spend a few hours and a challenging hike especially towards the top. Would recommend wearing good shoes/boots. Also best to go midweek if you can because it can get pretty busy up there at the weekends, although still less busy than Sigiriya Rock itself. Stunning views from the top, well worth it. Watch out for pesky monkeys at the top too, they'll try and rob you!
title: Brilliant hike

body: Our family of four hiked up Pidurangala Rock this morning and I have to say it was worth it. Our first day here we went to Sigiriya Rock and we could see people on Pidurangala. Our safari guide had also recommended it so after finding ourselves with some free time we went for it this morning. The first stage is bunch of steps (1238?) at the end of this you approach a nirvana Buddha. After this you go through a rock scramble to make it to the summit. If you are used to hiking this is easy, as was the case for me and my family. You have to pass through a temple at the base to get to the trail - no shoes or bare shoulders and knees here so cover up. Also the fee is LKR 500/person - children under a certain age are free. In the end it was a fun excursion. Many people do it so you will have company, including devotees of all ages who were climbing up barefoot or in flip flops.
title: A hike worth doing if you’re able to

body: This rock is in front of the lion rock. It lacks the gardens and the statues but the nature and the views are amazing. For 500 rs you'll have an amazing experience and take some nice pictures.
title: Cheaper, still great

body: Follow the red arrows to get to the top. Scramble over rocks / under rocks / between rocjs. Difficult for small kids although they will easily get to the reclining Buddha. Fantastic view of Sigiriya. Sigiriya is expensive but imo totally worth it. Great to be able to see Sigiriya from Pidirangula
title: Well worth the climb!

body: We left Kandy to go to pidurangala rock at 3am in order to get here to watch the sunrise, and it was definatly worth the early wake up call! Although the hike is slightly challenging it is amazing once to you get to the top to watch the sunrise! A few snaps from up the top below!
title: Hike for the sunrise

body: we had an good experience of hiking Pidurangala Rock and there was lots of wind on top of the rock..
title: Perfect hiking..

body: It’s a trickier climb but honestly so much more fun. Sigiriya is SO EXPENSIVE. $30 just to climb and take pics. Pidurangala is only 500 rupees and is so so fun! The views are also un...real!
title: Skip Sigiriya and climb this instead

body: Should not miss this if you are travelling to Sigiriya and surroundings. Nice Hike and amazing sunset.
title: Amazing Location

body: It is a normal trend among travellers to visit both the Sigiria rock and Pidurangala rock one after other on consecutive days.Its always better to climb up the rock eaely morning as possible as it will help you to explore the beautiful nature before the sun reaches top. If you reach on top before sunrise then you will be blessed with one of the awesome view of sunrise as well as can witness the rays falling on Sigiria rock.Compare to Sigiria the entry fees is very less and worth a climb.As I mentioned in header it is more of a untouched attraction which helps nature lovers to explore it with more peace.A small stretch with very big rock stone will be a task to cross but fellow traveller will definitely help you to cross and encourage if needed.This rock climbing is more of a trekking experience to the top then some scary man made stairs and platforms made on Sigiria.A must visit if you are in Sigiria town.
title: Untouched compare to Sigiria rock

body: Pidurangala Rock is a massive rock in the middle of an otherwise flat area, where only Sigiriya also towered up above the surroundings.Pidurangala is a more difficult hike than Sigiriya, but also less visited by tourists.The view from the top of the rock is truly breathtaking and was a complete 360 degree panoramic view of the area as far as the eyes could see.One of the main focal points of the view is of course Sigiriya Rock, which is located fairly close to Pidurangala and it was very interesting to see the rock from a different angle.In general Sri Lanka as a travel destination was a wonderful place with very friendly people, so beautiful nature and a very interesting cultural heritage. We travelled a few months after the Easter Sunday bombings, but we felt very safe throughout our trip and everyone we met were very welcoming and happy to have tourists visiting their cities, cultural sites, attractions and hotels.
title: Beautiful panoramic view of the surroundings and Sigiriya Rock

body: You shouldn't leave Sigiriya without doing this climb. It's without a doubt, the best view in the area and only costs 500 rupees per person compared to over 5000 to climb Lion Rock.The walk takes 30-45 minutes at a moderate pace and is a little bit tricky towards the end with boulders to climb to get to the top but it's definitely worth it.There's a monastery at the entry point where you need to cover your knees and shoulders. If you don't bring coverings, they have spares near the entry which you can wear while you walk through the monastery to the point where the actual climb begins.
title: Can't miss it

body: This was my third time climbing the rock. I always prefer climbing Pidurangala than Sigiriya. It is less crowded in the early morning and it would be perfect if you can be on the top for the sunrise.
title: Best View!!

body: went right around sunset and it was absolutely beautiful everybody should do the hike l feel like. breathtakking view up top makes you forget about everything....
title: beautiful view

body: The climb to this rock is challenging. Make sure you have someone to accompany you as navigating the rocks and path is difficult. We had our driver Dasun walk with us. He was excellent in guiding us with the safest way to climb the last part of the trek. This part has no path just a variety of rocks to climb, crawl and step up and over. The view from the top is worth the 30 min trek. You can relax and find a spot to enjoy the view of Sigiriya Rock and the surrounding landscape with the sunset. There were lots of tourist enjoying the tranquility of this place. The trek down is easier. Don’t leave it till it gets too dark.
title: Great sunset spot

body: One needs to 'work' to climb up this Rock. Free for those citizens of Lanka, it costs about LKR 500 for an overseas visitor. There is a general distaste for people who wear short trousers and singlets, One is warned that proper attire is required to pass the portals of the temple (supposedly of the 5th century CE) which is at the ground level, and through which precincts one can access the steps and gullies that allow one to get to the top of the rock. There are encouraging posts that informs one of the number of uneven and often steep steps to climb, but, those exhortations are only estimates!!! When one 'set of steps' are done, hey presto around the next bend are 280 more of those steep steps until the next level, and then there are more!!! All quite fun- unless one is prone to heart seizures. The final 'assault' is quite tricky, unless one is supple and agile. It involves creeping on one's belly to get past the narrow apertures betwixt rocks, and then.....relief, as one enters the plateau with the most magnificent 360 view of the surrounding plains and the Sigiriya rock monument up ahead. Very strong gusty winds will test your already exhausted frame to remain standing!! Great experience, great physical exercise!!
title: Not an easy amble up a rock!

body: We did this walk at around 3.30 pm I had wanted to go for sunset but ticket office closes at 4.30pm so my driver advised against it , however what I discovered was that, we could of bought tickets at 4.30 pm and do the climb and be there for sunset , however this didnt happen! The climb gets tricky at the end and you have to climb through some rocks but it is very doable.. the views are amazing even better than Sigiriya as you can see Sigiriya from there and you can also walk along the top of Pidurganala. It is very cheap in and it is really worth it. When we were walking down we met loads going up for sunset and I would say it is the busiest time !
title: Lovely climb and beautiful scenery

body: Go early in the morning to watch the sunrise.The last part of the climb is a little bit tricky therefore not recommended for people who arent fit or for young children
title: Beautiful sunrise

body: We came here on our first evening in the area (before visiting Lion Rock). Ideally you have time to do both, but if you could only fit in one, it's hard to call. Pidurangala is much cheaper, and crucially, much less crowded.It's a tough walk up at any time of day. The scramble up some rocks after the path finishes is more challenging than I expected but my wife (despite not being tall) was still able to make it over. We did decide not to stay for the actual sunset as we thought the walk down in the dark and amongst fairly large numbers of people, would have been unpleasant.Nonetheless, we enjoyed great early evening views of Lion Rock and the surrounding area.
title: Great view of Lion Rock

body: Awesome little place. For me, it's the best of the 2 visits. That's cheaper. Shorter (Even if the last part of the walk/climb is a bit tricky, but we've seen some old local people doing it). And you got this amazing view on the rock ! What else do you want ? GO FOR IT !
title: Best of the 2.

body: Definitely worth tackling the slightly treacherous path in the dark to sit atop this rock and marvel at the splendid views. Another spectacular Sri Lanka experience
title: Gorgeous sunrise

body: Beautiful spot and not too long of a climb. If you're in the area, it's worth going for the view. The top bit could be tricky for anyone with injuries/knee problems but take it slow and you'll be fine.
title: Go up for the Sunrise

body: The entrance fee was very low for a wonderful climb in the sunrise. It was not very busy and the view of the lion rock was unique. Bring something to cover yourself because there is a temple at the entrance.
title: Quick climb and great view

body: For the best views of Sigiriya this walk is a must. We went for sunrise and the walk itself is pretty easy, only around 20 minutes to the top, staircases and a little bouldering at the end make it fairly accessible for most people. The path itself has a few lights going up but we took headlamps too which did help going before the sun was up. Once up top the view is incredible, not just of Sigiriya but the whole area, we had a walk around and sat down for the sunrise with maybe 40 other climbers. Would love to do it for sunset too. Definitely worth the climb!
title: Super Sunrise

body: Don’t trust Google Maps, this place is open till late and you can watch the sunset! We had a lot of fun climbing, but keep in mind the path is not well built like Sigiriya rock, and has a few parts where climbing is not so easy. It is worth going to the top as the view is amazing!
title: A lot of fun to climb this rock

body: I had thought we would be going up the rock around 4ish because of the heat, but ended up there around 2pm. Our driver said it was ok as most of the way up was in shade. That was true. We went with our kids 7 & 11 years old. After reading the reviews I was worried about the last part with the kids but there was nothing to worry about as it was like an adventure for them, not hard at all! Most of it in shade. The views are amazing and looking at Sigiryia rock was lovely. Very windy up there but pleasant because of the heat. The way down was very entertaining as the kids loved seeing all the monkeys with their babies!
title: I thought it was going to be harder

body: This is not the Lion Rock. This is not Sigiriya. This is a rock on a hill nearby from which you can view Sigiriya. When I was researching I found a lot of the reviews for Pidurangla were actually talking about Sigiriya. Beware! This is a shorter climb, much cheaper, than Sigiriya. You get a good view of Sigiriya and the valley. It is about 15 minutes to the first view of Sigiriya if you don't need to stop and rest. The last bit of the way up there are large rocks you have to scale and then squeeze through a small crack. There is no avoiding this. I don't know how people do it in the dark. I would have a hard time before sunrise. There were lots of flip flops lost in cracks wear proper shoes, it will go far easier. Basically I would like to warn if you can't scale say a 1m rock by pulling yourself up do not bother with this climb at all. You will not have good views until after the hard part. Reasonable fit looking people were having difficulty with the heights. It was a nice view and breeze at the top so a nice attraction. We had 2 days in Sigiriya so had the time. There are good views of the rock in town too. If stairs and climbs are hard for you I do not think you should push yourself here, it is not a must do. I went late afternoon around closing time there were lots of local groups so a bit of a crowd at the squeeze through the crack part. The first bit is a temple so you have to take off your shoes and cover your legs and arms there are loaner skirts for this purpose.
title: A bit of a scale and squeeze at the end

body: We chose to climb this rock instead of paying the $30 to climb the "big rock" because the price was only 500 rupees (if I remember correctly) and you get an incredibly view of the other rock. It was certainly hot climbing the steps and rocks (near to the top), but the route wasn't busy and the views were well worth it! I really feel sorry for those who were queuing on lion rock!
title: Amazing view!

body: Great view of Lion Rock and a lot cheaper. Path can be challenging in parts near the top as there is some climbing over and around rocks (but a couple made it with a nine month old baby on his back so obviously achievable). Amazing view from the top. For those who enjoy a bit of exercise in the heat it is well worth the trip (we did this as well as Lion Rock). Don’t forget to take water. Also at start you walk through a Buddhist temple so have to take shoes off for a small part of the walk and women need to cover shoulders and wear clothes that cover their knees. Once past the temple you can put shoes back on and wear shorts etc.
title: Great vista of Lion Rock

body: Lion Rock was amazing - over 1000 steps to reach the top - tough climb. We did the extra steps to view the ancient paintings - well worth it. What an amazing place to put a palace!
title: Lion Rock hike

body: We came here for the sunrise and were not disappointed! We needed about 25 minutes to the top. A flashlight is necessary for the last 300 steps because after there are no lights on the way anymore. The last 20 meters you have to climb over rocks but it is not too difficult. Even not well trained people are able to do it. The 360 view was very great!
title: Nice View! Great sunrise!

body: Breath taking view of Sigiriya rock and can't express the beauty of nature by word! You should climb pidurangala rock to experience that!
title: Just Amazing!!

body: Truly amazing place to visit. I must say MUST visit.. the view is breath taking.....You never want to come back.. Soak in to the nature.... You can see magnificent Sigiriya rock from there. Best view ever..
title: Door way to heaven

body: Pidurangala Rock is adjacent to Sigiriya Rock and is the best viewing point of Sigiriya Rock. Pidurangala is a popular spot for 360-degree views. make sure to take your all camera gears to capture more fascinating and memorable seance.
title: if your more into hiking

body: It’s an easy hike. Best time to hike would be around 4.30pm. Then you can see the perfect sunset. Check the sunset time before you go and then start the hike accordingly. It’s just a 45 min hike.
title: I would prefer Pidurangala over Sigiriya Rock

body: the view of the surronding and the rock is breattaking. Due to the bombing one month ago, the place is very quiet. Perfect time to go for sunrise !
title: Choose there over the lion rock

body: This is just 1-2 km north from Sigiriya citadel (Rock). Pidurangala looks like a twins of sigiriya. The entrance ticket is 500/= (LKR) (2.5 $) for foriegners. Climb to start rock is through ancient buddhist temple. Its take only 30 minutes to climb the top. Better wear comfortable shoes.Basically there are 2 stages to climb this rock, first stage is easy as there are man made steps. Once you walk this phase you will see the rock caves where monks who lived 2000 years ago and a huge lord Buddha's stratue. The second phase is bit different to climb as there is no organized steps or path. But when you climb to top you will see the iconic view of sigiriya from air. Im sure you forget all the tiredness. The topof the rock there is a ruins of old stupa and some buildings.
title: Best place to see Sigiriya Citadel

body: Pidurangala and Sigiriya like looks twins from far, distance between them around 2 km. Entrance to Pidurangala starts from temple, entrance ticket for foreigners coast 500 rs, free for locals. It's important to wear comfortable clothes and shoes, take water and sun protection cream, climbing up around 30 minutes. There's a statue of lying down Buddha on the way. There are not organized rocks at the last part of climbing. Iconic view of Sigiriya is really beautiful and fantastic. Our other group of friends went to Sigiriya, so we called and waved to each other from the tops of mountains. It was unforgettable memories and experience.
title: Iconic view of Sigiriya

body: We all visited this place as our guide said it really worth going. We just thought it could be tiring though. But once we were all top of this place and having the astounding view of the Lion Rock, we forgot all our tiredness. This is a great site to visit. !
title: Greatest look of Sigiriya Lion Rock

body: Once on top, the views are stunning but prepare to go for a long walk and enjoy the breath taking journey.
title: Stunning View

body: The entrance fee is only 500 rupees here vs US$30 for Sigiriya Rock. The hike is fairly easy except for the last part before reaching the Rock (need a bit of climbing, but not too difficult). Took me only 15 mins to reach the top where you have a great view of the surroundings and the Sigiriya Rock. Would suggest to do both if you are in Sigiriya.
title: Easy hike and great view of Sigiriya Rock

body: It's not easy to get one the peak. A bit difficult entry for disabled person or peoples afraid of heights. Path is exhausting especially during hot weather. But the views rewards hard climbing. Great place to see the majesty and unique of Sigiriya. A can't agree that it is alternative to Sigiriya, Pidurangala Rock is fantastic complement of Sigiriya!
title: Best place to see Sigiriy'a

body: Majestic Rock. 1200 steps to climb. We didn't climb as the younger one will not be able to do that and it was extremely hot. Entry charges are 50$ for foreigners. Everywhere in Srilanka this seems to be the norm and i find it on the higher side for this rock climbing. Anyway we hired a TukTuk and the driver Sajith took us around major viewpoints and explained the details. I recommend this to all those who cannot climb.
title: Majestic Rock

body: This was one of the highlights of our visit to Dambulla. The grounds are large and there are moats filled with water and water lillies. As one approaches the mountain, the size can be deceiving. Look carefully and you will see steps half way up near the center and you may catch a glimpse of other tourists making their way up. That will help give scale to the mountain. This is not for the faint of heart, people with a fear of heights, or someone who is out of shape. The stairs have parts that are steep and in the afternoon heat, it is practically unbearable. Bring water or something cool to drink. Half way up on the side are the lions paws. This is a nice place to take a rest and a few pictures before heading up the last set up steps to the top, where the 360 degree view is incredible. Beware of monkeys who try to steal drinks and snacks, and hold on to your bags very carefully because they aren't afraid to try to take it and run.
title: Lots Of Stairs But The View Is Worth It

body: This is one of the beautiful aria in Sigiriya. It's about 30-40 minutes climb on the rock. Stairs are there but at the last stage it's bit difficult to find stairs but rocks. Best time is to visit during morning hrs. Opens at 5am. Nearly 4 hrs drive from colombo.
title: Lovely Place to visit

body: Literally breath taking - Its a long way up and I must admit, I struggled a bit in the heat and after 4 days of inclusive meals.. But after about 30 mins of climbing steps and stopping...I arrived at the top. The views were amazing. Truly breath taking.Then the best part... meeting all the monkeys on the way up and way down..not aggressive and are literally an arms reach away.The walk down was easier than the walk up..gravity did help..lol..!!
title: Breath taking

body: We walked to the top of Pidurangala for sunset and views of Sigiriya rock and it was stunning!The walk itself was easy with the exception of the last few minutes where you scramble up about 20m or scramble and climb with the help of a rope. Its absolutely fine for anyone with decent fitness and kids should be OK if they are a bit older (there were loads of school kids). The total climb, according to my Garmin was 164m so not horrific. However, to get to the top of the rock you need to dress conservatively and briefly remove your shoes while you pass through a temple.Once on top, the views are stunning - you get a great view of Sigiriya and the surrounding area. It's easy to walk around as the surface is flat/at a slight incline. It doesn't matter if you don't get the perfect sunset as it is beautiful enough already. Even on a crowded day there is plenty of space for an uninterupted view due to the slope.One piece of advice, make sure you do head down before it gets to dark so you can navigate the trickiest part of the descent before it gets dark.
title: Great place to come for sunset/sunrise and great views over Sigiriya

body: I was a bit concerned having read all of the reviews ,and I have to say you need to be open to a bit of scrabbling if you are to reach the top but the views are fantastic ,you need to pick either an early morning ,or late afternoon due to the heat ,but you will be rewarded with a great view.Water is essential to do this climb,and watch your footing on the way down it can be misleading as the steps vary in height and withsIts a bargain compared to other sites and attractions, we saw a tree snake on the way down ,just to quick to take a photo ,perhaps next time ?
title: Fantastic exsperiance

body: It's a bit hard climb in the final section, you get 360 degree view. It's a nice experience compared to Lion's rock. No souvenirs, along the way, just a few tourists and locals.
title: Lovely view

body: Our driver let us choose between the 2 rocks to climb but steered us towards Pidurangala on price. We liked it being uncrowded. We have 3 different levels of fitness in our family... super fit, medium and zero...all of us were comfortable with the hike. At the start of the hike you walk through a temple so your knees and arms need to be covered. Then it’s up. Take your time. Enjoy the shade. It’s still very hot. Stop lots if you’re not fit. The reclining Buddha was apparently damaged by treasure hunters many years ago. The brick is the repair work done. When you’re nearly at the top of the hike there is some actual rock climbing to do. But it’s very manageable. When you come out of the rocks the view is fantastic... as well as feeling very pleased with yourself for choosing to keep going! Don’t be in a rush to go down. Explore the plateau. Beautiful panoramic views. As said, morning is the best time. One of our favourites.
title: Worth the sweat

body: Amazing place for see Sigiriya rock fortress and old history of kingdom. Try to avoid more hot time period and go in early morning or evening to see best view.
title: Amazing view !

body: Our children (5 and 7) complained about the heat, but otherwise did the walk with no concerns (the last 10 minutes involves scrambling over rocks, there is no path). There are great views from the top to Sigiriya. We also climbed Sigiriya, if you are reasonably fit you could do both in the one day. We paid 500 RPS per adult but nothing for the children.
title: Great climb

body: Pidurangala is a rock temple next to Sigiriya. It gives you a great photo of Sigiriya in the morning. You will see a 3rd century statue of the reclining Buddha which the plaster has all washed away. The best time to climb it is at the crack of down to be there for the sun rise. The climb to the top it not that easy, but once you get there you enjoy a 360 degree panoramic view of the whole area.
title: Tour

body: Best view on Sigiriya's rockWorth the climing!!Don't forget to bring you own water to the topNeed to cover your shoulders and legs at the begging cause you are in a temple
title: Best view on Sigiriya's rock

body: Sigiriya or Sinhagiri or even Lion Rock is an ancient rock fortress located in the northern Matale District near the town of Dambulla in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. This ‘rock’ is now World Heritage listed and considered one of the eight Wonders of the World, and this is quite fitting. Massive is one adjective you could use to describe Sigiriya, and massive it is. And by massive I also refer to the 200m climb to reach the summit. Well over 2000 steps up, and again down...... Is this monumental climb worth it - absolutely it is. You will be tired and sore but happy as.
title: Wow

body: Best place to have a great view of Sigiriya. You have to climb for around 30 mins if you need to go to the top which is totally worth.
title: Best view of Sigiriya

body: Pidurangala Rock in Sigiriya Sri Lanka is a must for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. It is an amazing natural rock. You must climb, but, it is well worth it when you get to the top. The view is magnificent.
title: Pidurangala Rock in Sigiriya Sri Lanka

body: This is the free and rough cousin of Sigiriya and the view from the top is outstanding, but there is a bit of gentle rock climbing at the top. You enter through a Buddhist temple so have to cover your knees to go up - be prepared or rent a sarong on-site
title: More of a hike than we expected!

body: We woke at 4:30am to be taken up here by our tour guide.. we didn’t really know what to expect at the time as he hadn’t made to much fuss about it, but wow, it was incredible, and the view of Lions Rock is brilliant from the top.Make no mistake, the climb is pretty tough, so if you don’t have a reasonable level of fitness you’ll struggle, as when you get towards the top it’s not a straightforward hike, but it’s definitely worth it for the views. High on my list of must do’s in SL!
title: Awesome!

body: Best place to go for a hike in sigiriya. challenging for the elderly but if you take your time to climb to the top its worth while the visit and the view from the rock. a hot spot for many traveling to sigiriya.
title: next best rock to sigiriya and hiking

body: We opt to climb Pidurangala rock as it was way cheaper than Sigiriya Rock and it was really worth it. There is a small temple at the entrance before you start climbing hence you will need to take off your shoes & hat if any before you start. The climb suits anyone of any age till you reach the reclining Buddha statue. The climb from there on is a bit more challenging as you will need to squeeze yourself thru narrow openings and climb onto rocks (not steps) to go up. However, once you are up on top, you will have a stunning view of the area and the Lion rock. Look at the pictures and you will know what I'm saying. Well worth the efforts.
title: Stunning view on top!

body: I was one of a family party of 6. Our driver (who was our font of all knowledge) didn't just take us and say climb it, he gave us all of info about many other parts of this site prior to climbing it. It is high, and takes awhile. My advice is take your time, don't feel pressured by those going quicker than you, and do it as early as you can as the sun gets very very hot the closer you get to lunchtime. The views are amazing once you get to the top. Legs are pretty achy and feel quite wobbly after this climb but it's worth it! Before and after the climb you will, getting people trying to sell you things which of course you are entitled to purchase but they do hike up the prices for tourists, be aware, this applies generally for the whole of Sri Lanka though, and don't be afraid to barter, they will drop the price rather than lose the business in most cases.
title: Visit to climb Sigiriya Rock

body: We climbed at 5am with our two children in time for sunrise. A beautiful view of Sigiriya rock, fairly straightforward climb if you go slow (and take water!) and the view is totally worth it.
title: Beautiful hike for sunrise

body: Much cheaper than the main lion rock. A bit of a scramble up at times, but most fit/able people can manage it. Great views and mostly shaded walk. Recommend going around 6am to avoid the sunrise crowd and it will be more quiet up there.
title: Beautiful view!

body: Worth waking up early to watch the sunrise at the top. It’s not as long as Sigiriya, and has a great view of it from the top, it’s much cheaper as well. I was told I had to cover myKnees and shoulders and was given wraps, but lots of people at the top were in shorts and tanks. I’d recommend (for girls) wearing leggings and a T-shirt as the wraps made you quite warm.
title: Go for sunrise!

body: An impressive rock on which there used to be the king’s palace built in the 5th century. Now there are only foundations of these buildings left. Metal walkways are steep and narrow, which might be a challenge for somebody. It’s definitely worth to climb on the top of the rock, as the view is amazing, although in a hot day it’s not an easy walk.
title: One of the best places we visited in Sri Lanka

body: Highly recommend climbing this rock before you decide if you will climb Sigiriya Rock. This climb is manageable and worth it, especially at sunset. There's a little scrambling over rocks right at the end just as you reach the top but mostly it's a pleasant climb.
title: Great view of Sigiriya Rock.

body: the rook fabulous to climb not for the light hearated lost of steps and a few smail nooks to crawl throung but views at the top are well worth the hail
title: good viess

body: There's also no rocks unlike there are at Lion Rock! Do the sunrise hike, it's about £8 to get up and the walk is exciting, some of it is steps and some of it is climbing over rocks but the views at the top are so worth it!
title: The better rock to visit, cheaper, exciting climb and amazing views.

body: Our B&B owner presented both Pidurangala Rock and Sigiriya Rock Fortress to us. We chose Pidurangala because:a) It cost a fraction of the price (500 LKR per person, compared to 5,200 LKR to climb Sigiriya). b) We preferred the opportunity to see the view of Sigiriya Rock from the top of Pidurangala. Both rocks are located close to each other, in the Sigiriya region, so you could of course do both, if you have the stamina. Pidurangala is known as the more strenuous of the two climbs. It is a steep walk, and some parts do not have steps. It took us about 45 minutes to reach the top. We are both reasonably fit. The sights at the top are stunning. There are some small shaded areas where you can sit and enjoy the view of the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. The 360-degree views of the lush green Sri Lankan landscapes are well worth the climb. Note: Ladies are required to cover legs and shoulders at the entrance to Pidurangala, as visitors have to walk approx 25m past a temple before you start the climb. Scarves are available to borrow free of charge.
title: Breathtaking yet affordable views at Pidurangala

body: this rock is fabulous to climb,not for the light hearted,lots of steps and a few small nooks to crawl through,but the views at the top are well Worth the hall..
title: amazing climb and wow the views

body: If I had to choose between Pidurangala and Sigiriya rocks, I'd go with Pidurangala for 2 reasons 1. The climb is amazing!!! The path is not very well defined and you need to climb on rocks and take risks to go on top. 2. The view of the Sigiriya rock from here is stunning! You need to be quite fit (the ticket also says so) to reach on top. The climb till the Reclining Buddha is easy. Beyond that you're on your own! It's great fun if you like such activities. The view of the Sigiriya rock is just amazing!
title: Absolutely amazing!

body: My partner and I climbed to the top for sunset and were very glad we did. The climb wasn't bad at all - it gets a bit tricky on the second part of the climb so make sure you wear sensible shoes, however we did meet a few people wearing flip flops who managed okay. If you do climb for sunset, make sure you have a torch for the way down as it gets dark very quickly. Also Pidurangala Rock is considerably cheaper to climb than Sigiriya (Lion) Rock.
title: Beautiful sunset

body: It’s a MUST! You have to go visit. It was quite a bit difficult if compare with Lion Rock but it’s worth to go. It was beautiful up there with incredible view. You’ll see the Lion Rock from the top of the hill. Nothing to describe, see it yourself. Recommended 👍🏾
title: Stunning!

body: It takes about 30 minutes to climb and probably about 10mins to drive from the town to get to the bottom. Wear trainers as there are parts where you are climbing steep rock. At the top go left on the rocks as it’s easier and it’s also a good spot for photographing the rock without being in the crowds.
title: Great for the sunrise

body: bring decent shoes, water and easy to climb in clothes as there are huge boulders to climb over near the top. It is well worth the effort as you have an amazing view of Sigiriya and the surrounding forest
title: unexpected climb up Pidurangala

body: Everyone thinks that this rock is second to Lion's rock, however the view from the top is breathtaking. Be prepared for some tricky climbing nearer to the end/top!It is stunning as you not only get a 360 degree view of the city but also have the Lion's Rock in sight.So yes please wear proper footwear and get a ride to the rock as it can be an hour walk to it from Sigiriya Village. Thumbs up the review if it was helpful!
title: Exceeds your expectations

body: No doubt that this is one of the most unique and beautiful site my two eyes have ever seen! Its only a few rupees, and very few people were there.The hike is steadily up on stone steps, and a little trickier once you get closer to the top and the big round boulder. There you need to wedge your feet against the wall, and pull yourself up on the top rock platform. Once up there, there are just no words to describe the beauty all around! The views of the Sigiriya rock are even better then the views from the rock itself. Just absolutely breathtaking and spectacular! I'd recommend bringing also me water and a little bit of food as they're are a few very sweet errand dogs up there. No doubt my favorite experience in all of Sri Lanka!!!
title: ASTONISHING!!!!!

body: We arrived at 6.30am when it opened as our guide said we don't want to do it in the heat and the queues. Glad we listened! We passed the queues on the way down! It's over 1200 steps to the top and quite tough. Took us around an hour although 20 minutes to get down! Great views at the top but take plenty of water!
title: Tough trek to the top!

body: I climbed this immediately after coming down from Lion Rock. the sun was well up but most the climb is in the shadePlease don't be one of the disappointing number who ignore the signs about removing shoes and hats for the 5 minutes it takes to walk through the temple at the bottomIt's simple though mildly strenuous climb for the most part, until you get to the last bit when you have to scramble up some pretty big boulders. It was far from crowded, but there were enough people giving each other help up the biggest boulders that you could definitely do it on your own.The view from the top is spectacular, and of course you get a great view of lion rock and all the people queuing for the stairs on it as they didn't start early enoughI was up and down, including a good while taking photos at the top in 40 minutes
title: Different from, but as rewarding as, Lion Rock

body: We opted to climb here instead of Lion’s Rock and I’m so glad we did. As previous reviews have said, entry is through a temple and you do need to cover up and take your shoes off. The climb is tough - ish, there is some rock climbing at the end, but if you’re able bodied and of reasonable fitness you’ll be able to manage it. The views are stunning and it is far less crowded than I imagine Lion’s Rock was, at one point there was less than 10 of us up there. At 500 RS each (about £2.50) it was a much cheaper alternative too.
title: Stunning

body: Stunning is the only word. Steep climb but worth every step. There are local men who can assist you for a fee. Well worth their help as I have very bad knee and my helper was invaluable. Don’t give up take is slowly and enjoy breath taking scenery
title: WOW a must to visit

body: The beginning of the hike is easy and it starts from a Temple (long clothes & no shoe or hat at the beginning). At the end of the hike, you need to be a little bit fitter to put yourself up and go through rocks but that is still alright with kids as we saw some families up there.This is the best place in my opinion to see Sigirya and it is much cheaper too. The view on the top is amazing with a panorama on the forest and on the Sigirya’s Rock. The sunset is also amazing.
title: Stunning Panoramic View

body: It was really amazing experience and of course really tough way, at the part when you want to reach the end the way is really tough mountain climbing , and i also saw a snake attack to a lizard, really nice experience and i really love that, when you see a sigiria from this rock it is more beautiful i think.
title: Just wow

body: Even though Sigiriya archeological complex is probably the no.1 tourist attraction in Sri Lanka, we opted to climb the more budget-friendly Pidurangala Rock as it is the best viewing spot of Sigiriya/Lion's Rock (and the surrounding valleys).Of course, sunrise and sunset can be hit or missed depending on the weather, but this 30 minutes hike is surely worth your effort. Last part of the climbing is a little challenging. Time to the top of the Rock: 20/30 mins.Sneakers (and a great camera) are highly recommended.Entry ticket: 500 LKR per person
title: Budget friendly hiking

body: My partner and I climbed the rock leaving at 4:45 and made it up in 35 min, it is a rock step climb which turns tricky towards the end where it is more rock hopping than any thing else. Once up on top it feels like you are on top of the world, we waited for the sunset with about another hundred people - it was ok but....... The price of a ticket is 500 Sri Lankan rupees.
title: Sunset

body: There are many reasons to hike Pidurangala Rock. First, there is a major price difference between the neighboring rock. Sigiriya Rock can run you a bill of about $40/person CAD, while Pidurangala will only cost you 500 LKR ($3.65 CAD). Now, while the hike is a bit of a challenge, the effort is well worth it. We highly recommend sunrise as the views are breathtaking; the rising sun illuminated the vast wilderness below, the shadows made by the two large adjacent rocks and the birds chirping in the morning sun make it a spectacular sight. Definitely bring a head lamp, wear good shoes, and be ready to use all four limbs to climb at certain points!
title: A view that rocks!

body: The best thing about this place is that it's "local". Opposite to Sigiriya it's full of locals visiting this rock and not hordes of tourists like on the Sigiriya. From the top you can see the whole Sigiriya rock and honestly i think this view is even better than the most famous rock there. At the bottom there is an old buddist temple and also monk houses. You have 360 degrees view on the whole area around. In my opinion it's way better to visit this rock and not Sigiriya (unless you're a typical tourist) :)
title: Perfect view point

body: Pidurangala is a beautiful place in srilanka closed to sigiriya. Pidurangala rock is surrounded by a rain forest. You can see some ancient relics while you climb. Superb👍👍👍
title: Hidden beauty

body: Climbing the Sigiriya Rock was not something I was looking forward to but the experience was truly amazing...The views are out of this world. However, its a hike! Not just steps but steep, uneven steps with people pushing to go up and come down. We made it as far as the Lions feet but didnt do the spiral ladder on the outside of the rock to the top, it just looked too precarious to me.....My health and safety hat came on and we decided against it. Were we glad we did it...yes. Something to tell the grandchildren!
title: Not for the Unfit

body: Twin Brother of the Sigiriya rock. The second most famous place to visit when touring the sigiriya area.
title: Twin Peaks in Sigiriya

body: I had to choose between Lion and Pidurangala Rock and i opted for the last one.You only pay 500 Rupee (almost ten times less than for Lion rock), the climbing through the forest is fun, even though a bit challenging towards the end ( moderate effort ).Once you are above, you‘ll have a majestic view over the Lion rock and Sigiriya‘s surrounding.I was there for the sun set and it was not very crowded. Don‘t forget to take a bottle of water with you and please do not litter! I walked back down with at least ten plastic bottles. Very sad to treat nature that way.If you don‘t want to spend that much money for the entrance, I would definitely recommend Pidurangala rock. Enjoy the view!
title: The view!

body: Wear modest clothing as you walk through the temple at the bottom, but you’ll need trainers for the hike, flip flops won’t do. It’s 500 rupees so really cheap if you can’t afford the lion rock. Come up an hour or two before sunset, take lots of photos and soak up the views. The last 10 minutes of the climb is quite hard so try to stick with other people in case you need a hand or a little push!
title: Beautiful sunset

body: Wonderful adventure! Enchanting, Beautiful, not to be missed! Requires climbing around 20 minutes through exigent conditions the last 5 minutes. A lantern is of good help when dará.
title: Sunrise or Sunset

body: With a bit of courage you will be able to reach to the top..just go with a good health and never miss the view..the view is one of the best gift nature
title: Manama

body: We walked up the hill, at first the path was good, but then we had to climb over boulders and then we reached the flat top. The view was fantastic we could see the Pidurangala Rock and Sigiriya Citadel
title: Pidurangala

body: Bit of a difficult scramble when you get to the top but superb views .. don’t wear flip flops! There are lights on the path if you want to go for sunset but not sure if they turn them on ... ask at the bottom
title: Great and only 500 rupees

body: Far fewer people than the more famous Lion Rock, it provides fantastic views of the latter and the surrounding countryside. It is much more of a hike, with a mixture of rough steps and scrambling over rocks, so wear good shoes.
title: An alternative to Lion Rock

body: Wr climbed Pidurangala instead of Sigiriya rock because we had been told that it was much more sheltered and less busy, as well as being significantly cheaper (500 lkr per person). While the climb was quite challenging, especially towards the end, the views were amazing. I would definitely recommend this to anyone visiting the Sigiriya area, but make sure you bring decent footwear!
title: Beautiful veiws

body: We hired a personal driver to take us to the Pidurangala Rock from Colombo after climbing the Sigiriya Rock earlier that morning. This was around a four hour drive and we also visited the Dambulla Temple on this day.The Pidurangala Rock cost 500 rupees to climb (a fraction of the cost of Sigiriya [5400]) and was a very worthwhile but difficult climb. There are steps most of the way up but as you reach the peak you will be expected to clamber over some large rocks to reach the summit. But the views from the top are amazing and there is a perfect view of Sigiriya. It should also be noted that you must walk through a temple at the bottom before making your way up the rock so we were expected to cover up and remove are shoes for a short distance.
title: Worthwhile and value for money!

body: The google maps location is correct. You can park the vehicle and start climbing from the temple entrance. You cannot wear shorts or sleeveless tops when passing the temple (which is like aroud 50m) . As an aternative you can use shawls to cover those areas and remove them once you have passed the temple. The climb is quick. Around 20 minutes while taking breaks. The last bit of the climb is toughest where is the beginning is steps. The view is the best.
title: Worth the effort

body: I would recommend to go to pidurangala rather than sigiya rock ... the view is amazing and make sure u climb early in the morning (5am) so that you are on time for the sun rise. U defo don’t want to miss this. Also climbing in the morning is better as it might get too hot later. The prices are 5 times less for entry compared to the other rock. Make sure u were moderate clothing( recommended to wear long dress, trousers) as the entrance is through the temple. They do provide you with scarfs in case you are wearing shorts. I managed to get some great shots which I’m posting below.
title: Best view ever

body: Exactly one of the best place to watch sunrise, I didn't pay 5000 rupee to lion rock, I paid only 500 rupee to this rock and I watched one of the best sunrise in my life ever. It needs around 20 min to climb, but worth it. You can see the lion rock and take some great picture...
title: Great sunrise, don't miss it

body: This particular Rock is an alternative used by the monks as their place of worship and place of meditation. In history the monks used Sigiriya as their place of worship and meditation, But when the king at that time saw this awesome Rock wanted it as his Kingdom n requsted the monks to move to the adjoining Rock n they willingly obliged. And to date it is used by the monks of the present era.....it is extremely breathtaking to experience the sunrise and sunset...also enroute you find this exquisit chill Lounge serving the most flavourful Sri lankan cuisine with a touch off Fusion added so that the travellers can enjoy w/o too much spice and the coffee is excerlent too.....the place is called Laki's Lounge...
title: Awsome sunrise and sunset

body: Don't go to the Lion's Rock (where they just want to take your money) : this is too expansive, and for much much cheaper (500 rps if my memory is good against more than 5500 for the Lion's Rock) you have the same view at the top of the Pidurangala Rock - if not even more beautiful !
title: Cheaper and even more beautiful !

body: Visited Pidurangala rock As Sigiriya was too busy we opted for this site instead - isn’t as busy but the views were totally worth it - one of our most memorable sights - certainly well worth doing
title: Honeymoon trip

body: Having climbed Lion's Rock, we wanted to climb this one s well to get the view from the summit. We were not disappointed. In our opinion, the temple at Pidurangala, reclining Buddha half way up and the views from the summit equalled Lion's Rock, if not surpassing it. The last part is a bit of a scramble (wear trainers not flip-flops) and there are no guard rails anywhere to be seen which makes the summit more special. Look out for the snakes basking on the rock at the top!
title: Climb up Pidurangala Rock through the Rock Cave and Temple

body: Great way to see Sigirya Rock if you don’t mind not viewing the ancient palace ruins up close. It has amazing views and still has Buddhist carvings and a cultural vibe. We did not do Sigirya as we avoid crowds and lines to tourist attractions. Pidurangula is so much nicer to climb and it is huge on top, where you can roam about and are almost to yourself. Naturally, this is superior to Sigirya Rock in my opinion. Depends on your preference!
title: Go here for a cheap, stress free hike

body: We went to see the sunset and It was great because you have a complete view of lion rock that it is in front. The path is a little bit tricky in the end but not so difficult. The reward is worthy!! Another thing is that is cheaper than lion rock! It depends on tour budget!
reviewer_location: San Cristobal de La Laguna, Spain
title: Great view of lion rock

body: A great place to see the sunrise !From there also a good view on the Lion Rock. Don’t forget a torch :)
title: Sunrise !!!

body: The climb to the top on February 25, 2019 was not too strenuous, and it was nice seeing the temple at the beginning and the other lying down Buddha carving. The view from the top was surprisingly nice. You can walk around the top of the rock and see 360 degrees all around you. If gave a nice perspective of the topography, lakes, farms, and woodlands. The sunset view was very nice. It was worth the short hike to the top. I would do it again.
title: Nice Hike, Temple, and Sunset View

body: Very difficult rock to climb. Mountaineering skills required. Not for the faint hearted. But the view once the top is reached is spectacular.
title: Tour

body: We hiked the Lion rock on the morning and this rock in the evening, which I would highly recommend in that order! The Lion rock is really a great hike and a very historic site, but crowded and a lot of tourists, but if you go earky( before 8 am) you will avoid the crowds. This rock at pidurangala is so much cheaper! You go thru a temple first so bring a cover up, ( which you can remove as well after) and you have to remove your shoes, but can put them back on before you start the hike. There was mostly locals there and we went late afternoon. Everyone goes for sunset, which I’m sure is smacking but you would have apt more people there and may have to hike down in the dark which would be even more challenging! So bring a headlamp or flashlight if you decide to do that! We went at 4 pm which was a perfect time. The hike took us about 40 min, and we were going at a moderate pace. There are a lot of steps, and it’s pretty steep, but really not that hard. At the end you have to climb boulders to reach the summit! Fun, but a bit challenging for some, but we saw children and people on their 70s do it! So could you! Incredible views from the top! Better than Lion rock! If you have time, do both. If only time for one hike, do this one! Loved it!
title: Wonderful hike with stunning views!!

body: Really nice place. Can see the sigiriya rock in awesome angle. Short hike but interesting. Bit busy on weekends. Temple also there. Don’t forget to worship. Better to visit morning or evening
title: Nice View

body: Significantly more challenging than we expected to get to the very top, however the views were worth it and it gave a great sense of achievement. I recommend wearing proper walking shoes.
title: Worth the challenge

body: Much less crowded than Sigiriya. Approximately a 20min climb, but more challenging than Sigiriya. Towards the top there are large boulders and you will need all fours. Nice reclining Buddha halfway/ best time sunrise or sunset. Royal cave temple at start.You must take off your shoes to past the temple and can put them back afterwards to climb.
title: Wonderful views of Sigiriya (Lion Rock)

body: With a guide we walked up the many steps and do not forget you have to scale/clamber up the last part for a breathtaking view of the area including the adjacent rock Sigiriya!I would suggest going up there as early as possible due to possible crowds and the heat.If you are able bodied and moderately fit it is not a problem I did struggle with the heat but really enjoyed the challenge of the work out. There are no hawkers here trying to sell you anything and everyone around you will help you out if you need a hand up to the last part. If you run up you could do it in 15 minutes but take it easy and you are up in 25 minutes NOT the hour as advertised at the bottom of the Rock! Enjoy the moments up there as it is a truly one off wonderful view.
title: Top view nice place

body: Admission costs about three dollars. 20 min hike to the top, Go there at sunrise or sunset and you will be amazed.
title: What a view!

body: We climbed at around 11am this morning. 500 rupees entrance which is 5000 cheaper than Sirigiya! The brochure you get at entrance says "if you can climb Sirigiya then you can climb this"... definitely not the case. The walk up isn't particularly awe inspiring but not horrible however when you reach approx 10m from the top there's a pretty tricky climb. Sirigiya has steps all the way and nearly everyone could manage the climb however i can genuinely say not everyone will manage this last few steps which is a massive disappointment after hiking all the way up. A couple of people had to turn back as it was just too dangerous to attempt the final hurdle. That said, the view really is amazing once your at the top and in my opinion its better than Sirigiya with some great photographs to be had. It certainly wasn't busy like Sigriya was and there was an overall better atmosphere amongst the climbers.
title: great views but not an inaccurate brochure leads to confusion

body: We actually did this! We had to take off our shoes to cross a temple space before starting the climb up, up, and up. At the very end, it looked particularly difficult since we had to get around and through rocks. But we did make it to the top more or less flat rock where we could see the Lion's Rock from a distance. There were a lot of backpacker/kids at the top. After our arrival, a bunch of very young school groups arrived. While we were on the way down, a guide was scampering up to help his group, one of whom had had some type of incident. Make sure your guide goes with you! It is not an easy climb, especially toward the top and coming down.
title: We made it! even though we are old

body: Entry Fees: LKR 500/- per personThis is way cheaper than the Lion's Rock. Also I heard and read that this is a tougher trek. Lion's rock is more from the historical point of view and has steps almost till the top. The sunset view from the top is really amazing. There is quiet a lot of space to walk around on the top. The views of Sigiriya rock are also good. More or less both rocks offer similar view of Sigiriya and sunset/sunrise. Tips: Carry water, snacks, cap/scarf to cover from the sun (little shade available). Must put of shoes, the last part is climbing up the rocks. It is slightly tough not too much to do. Probably senior citizens can skip. There is a buddha temple at the entrance, so need to cover yourself like most other places in Sri Lanka. Donot carry any bulky items since it will be tough to get them through the small gaps in the rocks.
title: Tougher & cheaper than Lion's Rock

body: We climbed this rock to watch sunset, having heard that it was a much more unique experience than the main rock and much cheaper. To get there it is possible to walk (approx 4km), or take a tuk tuk/car, however, bare in mind if you haven't booked a return journey transport has a captive audience and double the cost for the return. If you walk back take a torch or walk a short way and the price reduces substantially! The initial climb goes through a temple where shorts are not permitted but they have sarongs you can borrow. The climb is quite awkward in places but short sharp shock rather than gruelling and takes about 20 mins if reasonable fit. The top of the rock is reasonable flat and the views are amazing. We shared the top with around 100 people but the experience was much more pleasurable than Sigiriya rock... and at 500 rupees much cheaper! If you can't get to climb the big rock do not see this as a poor cousin, in some ways it beats it hands down - great views and much more peaceful
title: Better view than Sigiriya Rock

body: Visit to climb for sunrise. Path is clearly marked until the top section which requires some scrambling, my head torch came in useful for this.Lovely to sit atop the rock and wait for day break. Great view of Sigiriya from the top too!
title: Climb for sunrise

body: My partner and I were tossing up whether it was worth making an extra trip from Kandy to Sigiriya at the end of our holiday after 10 days travelling in Sri Lanka. Wow, we were really glad we did! We climbed to the top of Pidurangala starting around 4.30pm to make sunset. I consider myself quite fit, and was surprised at how challenging the climb is especially towards the top where you need to navigate large boulders. Couldn’t believe people were doing it with small babies. Once at the top the view of Sigiriya and surrounds was magical. We left before sunset as we wanted to make sure we could hike back down before it was dark. If you have limited time and need a great driver to take you to Sigiriya from Kandy contact Inoon on +94 77 780 4004. He has English, and he really bent over backwards to meet our every request, and very reasonably priced at only 7500 rps per day. He really made our trip and I cant recommend him enough. So worth it to have driver to be waiting at the bottom of the mountain to take you around in air conditioning, rather than tuk tuk. A highlight of our trip, but definitely wear your hiking boots.
title: Wonderful experience, definitely worth it! Get ready for a challenging hike though

body: We woke up really early to see the sunrise. The path is well kept and signalised. Is not an extreme walk but the last few meters require a bit of skill. With luck you have a dog to guide you. In my opinion better view than the lion rock. The entrance fee is simbolic.
title: Amazing view

body: Having read some of the reviews, I was a bit nervous attempting this climb solo. Tourists pay Rs 500 in the temple complex at the bottom (where you need to be appropriately covered and remove your shoes when walking though the grounds). After that it's uneven stone steps up to the reclining Buddha. It's well shaded but still gets hot - overall however, not too challenging. After the Buddha you need to scramble over some boulders to reach the first ledge with a view over to Sigiriya. Following this it's a short uphill incline to the very top with views all around. As a solo traveller I just took it steady and it was not particularly difficult to find a route. There are arrows to help you or you can ask or watch those around you. The locals do it barefoot or in flipflops but I felt more confident in walking sandals. Overall, if you're a solo traveller don't let this put you off. It's completely do-able without help if you have an average level of agility, and if you do get stuck you can ask those around you.It's also an easy and pleasant walk from Pidurangala to Lion Rock if you fancy another climb! They are 2 very different experiences and I was glad I did both.
title: Fun and rewarding climb

body: Didn't want to pay for the lion rock and came here with my tuk tuk driver. Really nice walk and climb. I love the view from above. Very good place to meditate with a view of Lion rock in front of you.
title: Loved it!

body: Sigiriya Rock is the number one tourist attraction in Sri Lanka and this is also the main reason why most tourists travel to Sigiriya. In fact many other travelers I spoke to also agreed that Sigiriya Rock was great but it was Pidurangala Rock that was the more memorable experience.Like Sigiriya, Pidurangala was formed by volcano activity. Whilst Pidurangala appears larger than Sigiriya. It's upper surface is steeply sloped and is of solid rock. According to some travelers, climbing to the top of Pidurangala Rock is more strenuous than climbing Sigiriya. If you are fit and adventurous, it is a climb worth making and it took me 40 minutes to get up to the top. Proper footwear is strongly advisable.The climb can be divided into two stages. First stage climb has very steep irregular steps leading to a landing. This stage climb is strenuous but doable by fit people. Second stage is predominantly uncharted territory. It has no clear defined path or stairs. The second stage climb starts after the Reclining Buddha. It should only be attempted those who are fit and not obese. Size and fitness become a major issue here. We have to clamber up steers boulders and creep through very tight crevices. I was stuck once while trying to creep through one of the crevice. I felt a real sense of achievement when I got to the top after climbing more than 1500 irregular steps. I sat down in front of Sigiriya Rock waiting for a spectacular sunset. At the top of Pidurangala Rock, you will be greeted by a magnificent vista. Views from almost any angle, Sigiriya loom majestically. You can even see people climbing the stairs to the top of Sigiriya. On the highest point of Pidurangala Rock is a pile of rubble which is the remaining of the stupa. Climbing back down was a bigger issue, we need to go through whatever we did when climbing up but much harder. It was too crowded as everyone rushing to get down. I will say is pretty much slower as it was pitch dark and I was the only one who brought a very bright light which I used during my Audax cycling in Malaysia. The hardest hike I ever did but very rewarding.Entrance Cost: 500Rs
title: Cheap and Good

body: We decided to climb pidurangala rock to see a spectacular sunrise at the top.The climb started at 5.30am, and it was pitch dark.The first part of the ascent was easy, there were steps and lighting. As the ascent continued the lights were no longer available, so we used our mobile phone flashlights. The terrain became more challenging as the ascent continued, the very last few meters, we found really hard. We were helped by other climbers who explained the easiest way to continue our final ascent.I felt a real sense of achievement when I got to the top, and sat down in front of Lion Rock waiting for a spectacular sunrise.Unfortunately the clouds made sure we were not able to see the sunrise.We learned later sunsets are more likely to be visible as the clouds dissolve during the day.
title: I loved the experience and felt real sense of achievement at the top

body: My wife and I visited this very impressive rock together with a group. Our guide did inform us that there were some 1200 steps to the top of the Rock. As I am over 80 years old I felt that i may not make it to the top with the guide employed a local guide to carry my back pack, and help me up as far as possible. I was indeed quite adventure.On the way up there are some caves with very ancient wall paintings.When we reached the final stair case to the top I felt that's enough, and asked my guide to let us rest before the descent,I should add that I had had double knee replacement only 18 months before the adventure. My wife also employed a local guide and she did reach the top to view the ruins of he Palace
title: An adventure not to be missed despite age.

body: Wanting to avoid the crowds of Sigiriya we headed to this alternative. Climb not that difficult leading to fabulous views (including if one wishes of the hordes at Lion Rock). Got to the top c0830 and no more than a dozen others present.
title: Good alternative

body: Get an amazing view of Lions rock from the top of this place. The hike isn't long, we made it up in about 30-40min but the last part where you are bouldering can be challenging if you are old or not flexible. The hike is 95% shaded but at the top there is only limited coverage. It is far cheaper then the other option and not as busy at all.
title: Hard hike but very rewarding

body: its only about 500 rupees to get up this rock via the temple at the bottom, the first part of the climb are stone steps and paths , the last part is a scrambling climb UP boulders. If you go for sunset you will need a torch on the way down it gets dark. There are plenty of tuk tuks waiting at the bottom to take you back to your hote. TAke Water its a hot climb
title: great views from this cheaper ascent than Sigiriya
