body: Walk past the monastery (pay them a coin) and continue the hike to the top! The climb is not super easy but neither hard. The view from the top is priceless. We stayed until sunset and walked down with the small crowd and our flashlights. This hike was one of the highlights of our trip
title: A must do when in Sigiriya

body: the climb was a little bit more challenging than we expected. The last part to the top was a bit scary but we made it. The view from the top was worth the quickened heartbeat!
title: A bit of an aadventure

body: Visited both Pidurangala and Sirigiya on consecutive days. Loved both, but Pidurangala is a much quieter and serene.The climb is fun, and the views when you make it to the top are spectacular.If you're on a budget also worth remembering that Pidurangala is a fraction of the price of entering Sigiriya for an equally memorable experience.
title: Awesome

body: We have 4 kids (ages 2,4,6,8) and just recently did this hike...it was awesome. We are adventurous travelers but think that this is very doable for a family. Our 8 and 6 year old hiked the entire way by themselves. My wife carried the 2 year old in an Ergo Carrier and I carried the 4 year old in a backpack carrier.Prior to hiking we had a bit of an impression that it was dangerous or scary with kids but we didn’t think it was that dangerous. At the top the trail is not as well defined and is a bit more of a bouldering course with roots and rocks. At the very top the final entrance to the summit can be a tight squeeze so I had to take the backpack off and the 4 year old finished by herself and I handed the backpack through to my wife.All in all it was a very good hike, safety was not a concern and it was a rewarding feeling and the views were epic.The price is 500 Rupees/person and we even met a group from Uga and Back and Beyond that we’re up there volunteering their time to clean up the litter. It was great to see them taking care of the litter. Of course, much better if people would pick up their own litter but nice that they were helping pick up the slack.We chose to not do Lion’s Rock intentionally feeling that this was better option for our family and we felt very satisfied. Also, from the peak looking over at Lion’s Rock and the long line we felt that it was the right decision.Note: if it were raining this hike would be dangerous for a family for sure. The stairs on the way down (not up) are steep.
title: Awesome hike and able to do with young family

body: My driver dissuaded me from climbing Sigiriyar because there were like 1500 steps (and also I was with somewhat elderly parents and mum really couldn't climb), and provided us this option instead (500 steps thereabout). He forgot to mention the last part of the climb involved actual scrambling on rocks and hanging on to branches for support. There were moments I really wondered if people have died falling off the edges. (Mum gave up 5/6 of the way, and I felt bad for her)BUT, the view was worth it and I felt a real sense of achievement when I completed it. Furthermore, there were charming street dogs to accompany us on the way, and the air was fresh, so on the whole it was a very good experience!
title: It's not easy, but it's worth it

body: This rock is very beautifulAnd from here all the city can be seenEven the main rock is visibleIt gets shorter and easier
title: rock beautiful

body: Has go through the temple. Observe strict dress code. No bare knees shoulders or chest. No shoes or hats on the temple premises. But can wear them once pass the temple premises. Need good walking / hiking boots. Hard to moderate difficult climb as path has not been developed. Archaeological site. Reclining Buddha statue made of earthen clay by ? King Kassapa restored with bricks after been vandalised by treasure hunters. Climb is not for faint hearted. View from the summit is breath taking. The chief priest told us that King Kassapa made the temple and the Buddha statue so he can see from his rock fortress across.
title: Difficult climb up the rock but the view is fantastic.

body: A much cheaper option than Sigiriya just as breathtaking views but a more challenging climb. The last few hundred meters are difficult so say the least but if I can do it anyone could. It rained whilst we started the climb down making it slippery under foot. A worthwhile trip out but don’t be a hero and try to do the climb in record time. Just take it slow and pick your way. For me sometimes on my bottom
title: View of Sigiriya

body: The drive from the main tourist area to the start of the track is about 10 minutes. The entry fee is 1500 rupee.We did a sunrise hike but we didn't think to take torches, not smart on our part. It is quite a rocky climb, luckily people around us had their phone lights so we were able to find our footing.The sunrise is ok, a bit of smog and it's very short, you get a beautiful view of Sigirya. It takes about 40 or so minutes to climb. A great little walk
title: Take a torch

body: Very worthwhile climb . The last few meters climb is a scramble with the best path being the crawl through the gap between the rock and a precariously balanced boulder! There are other ways to get to the top but it helps if you are a mountain goat. A number of young tourist prefer to climb this rock rather than Sigiriya due to the $25 entrance fee charged for the latter. I think the Sigiriya climb is historically significant and cannot be substituted. This climb is complementary as it gives a perspective of the significance of the main rock and its ancient military/strategic position.
title: views make it worth the climb

body: Splendid view of the rock from this steep climb is worth it. The last meters are quite hard but there is enough space on the top
title: Great climb

body: This rock is facing the more famous Sigiriya Rock but it is also very interesting to see. First it is less crowded, because the last part of the way is quite demanding. Second, the view is asolutly breathtaking at sunset. Our best pics of our trip were taken from there!
title: Totally worth the climb!

body: As a preamble to Sigiriya Lion Rock climb we preferred this before cllimbing the famous Lion Rock. As both of us (my wife, aged 64 and I, 68) are seasoned trekkers, it was not at all challenging. In a sunny day it was quite impressive exercise. The view on the top was awesome with green shade everywhere. It was worth a visit.
title: Awesome climb and moderate climb.

body: We climbed this rock the day before climbing Lion Rock, and while it is slightly more difficult due to steps of varying heights and only having a pathway for roughly half the climb it I rate it higher than Lion Rock. There are far less tourists at any given time, and the views are equally if not more spectacular at sunset than Lion Rock. The last half of the climb past the Buddha statue can be a bit scary but it is definitely achievable. The entrance fee is also a pittance in comparison to Lion Rock at only 500 LKR. Definitely worth doing while you're in Sigirya.
title: Challenging but worthwhile climb

body: We chose to climb this rock with our tour guide as we didn’t feel we could manage the steps to top of Lion Rock, being height fearful, we were not disappointed as the bonus being we had a wonderful view of Lion Rock, there are still a number of steps to climb but not as many, the only hard part we found was the last 25 feet, as you have to clamber up over boulders and get on your hands and knees at one point. Well worth it but we ( late 50’s ) couldn’t have done it with help from our guide on that last bit. Everyone walks / climbs at different pace we took approx 40 minutes to climb. The views are exceptional including view over to Lion Rock. We stayed up there for another 40 minutes to catch our breath and then 30 mins to decend.
title: Great Alternative

body: We visited here as an alternative to Sigiriya Lipn Rock having read about it in our guide book and had both our hotel and tuk-tuk driver recommend it as a better option. OK, it’s not the big famous attraction but it’s only 500 rupees to enter compared to 30 USD at Sigiriya and had infinitely less people. Also, the view you get is pretty much the same as Sigiriya but actually includes the Lion Rock, which you don’t get when you’re standing on it.It’s a good stiff uphill walk for about half and hour with some scrambling over huge boulders just before you reach the top. The summit is huge and the 360 degree views are spectacular, including the view of Lion Rock and the continuous line of tourists climbing the metal staircase.
title: Great climb and stunning views

body: Lived in Sigiriya. We drove to Pidurangala at 03;00 pm . To see the sunrise. Less tourist place than Sigiriya. Entry is 500 LKR. per person.you must literally climb the boulders and there are no protections. Slightly dangerous but, the sight are very beautifull. Deserves asaolutely
title: Deserves asaolutely

body: Exhilarating even in the rain .an incredible place and well worth the effort.The best tip is to start at 7 am when it is cool and quiet ,people who went later talked of a giant queue which wasn’t much fun .
title: Exhilarating

body: it's the best place from where you can enjoy the best view of Sigiriya rock. It's really short but a little bit tricky walk. Totally worth it.
title: wonderful

body: This place is beautiful. High recommendation to climb this rock if you have the chance and you are fit enough. No worries tho, its not a long or too difficult hike. After buddha statue the path kinda disappeares and you need to climb over some stones and trees. Go with a friend and help each others if needed. View is stunning and early morning is the best time to go. P.s its not an excuse to give this place bad review if you are overweight and cannot make the hike. Its not Pidurangalas fault, its yours :)
title: Nice hike in the morning

body: Totally worth going to this place. We went early in the morning to see the sunrise but I recommend going there just after the sunrise as you can enjoy the walk more and see the Lion Rock nicely illuminated by the morning sun.
title: Incredible place

body: The climb up and down Lion Rock takes a couple hours. It's strenuous and not for people who aren't in good condition. Have a sweat rag to wipe your brow. Views from the top are spectacular. The ruins at the top are not great but they do show somewhat the layout of the palace with a couple remaining pools.
title: Exhausting climb

body: Yes, the hike is not as well paved as Lions Rock. The oath uneven, st times requiring hands to balance and some careful placement - but it’s mainky at the end and totally rewarded by the view of Lions Rock. It looks a bit surreal. Just breathtaking. You will need to walk barefoot up the stairs and cover until you pass the temple, and then you are free to hike as you were dressed. Absolutely amazing and so affordable, just do it!
title: Truly breathtaking - my favorite spot in Sri Lanka

body: We started at 05:00, the Tuk-Tuk was around 800/= including return. But the prices may change, check with your host when you order the driver. The entrance fee is only 500 /= - much more value for money thanthe 25$ for the Lions Rock. Of course, you won't be the only one climbing Pidurangala Rock, but compared to Lions Rock, it's deserted.The sunrise was magical: we saw the sky turn from pitch black to bright blue and the mist rising from the sea of trees below. Heared the distinctive sounds of the jungle waking up. Admired the morning sun over the Lion Rock. Pidurangala offers an amazing view across the jungle to Sigiriya with the Lion Rock rising above the tree line. One of the best views during our one month trip. It's a steep 20-minute uphill walk to the summit - mostly stairs but the last minutes you'll be climbing across rocks. Nothing complicated, but ditch the flip-flops in favor of comfortable shoes, pack a bottle of water, a torch and jump right into this adventure.
title: One of the most amazing views on Sri Lanka

body: Actually quite a quick walk: about 1 hour round trip including photo time.The bit after the Buddha gets scary as you have to boulder but actually it’s only for about 30m so suck it up and do it for the view. Views are amazing and unless you’re into temples and want to see the temple at Lion rock then definitely do this instead.
title: 100% must do

body: This climb did get difficult at points where you have to squeeze between rocks but the view from the top was absolutely beautiful! So worth it!
title: amazing view

body: We went up around 15.30 and it took us (senior citizens) half an hour to get to the top. The last bit was a scramble but doable. Entry fee is 500 rupies. In the morning we climbed Lions rock but this one gave us much more pleasure. Great view from the top. There is no better way to view Lions rock!
title: Better than Lions Rock

body: the 1200 stairs seem daunting but well worth the hike. Take your time to take in the magnificent views and the king's throne
title: great hike great views

body: A fairly challenging climb. Beautiful views. Ancient reclining Buddha statue near the peak. The steps are steep and the last 10 minutes of the climb is a difficult scramble over uneven boulders. The descent is hard. The views are. Spectacular
title: Pidurangala rock Sri Lanka

body: Definitely not easy peasy as someone described it, but I did manage it with wearing a dress and flip flops (which I don't recommend). It took us maybe half an hour to get up. Wear something to cover your shoulders and knees and take your shoes off when you go through the temple area. The last 10 minutes is climbing on rocks but nothing too difficult. Great view of Sigiriya and even though there were a lot of people we also found quiet spots. We went at midday, best time would be sunrise or sunset. We've also climbed Sigiriya which was maybe more impressive but of course a bit more expensive too. Have a cold coconut when you get down!
title: Amazing views

body: I wouldn't have climbed this rock if I wasn't with another (younger) couple but I am so glad that I did. After the crowds at Sigirya spoiling what would have been a wonderful climb, this was a much better experience. It was harder as there was no excuse for stopping as you are walking up the steps as no crowds, and there is a bit of scrambling when you get to the latter part of the climb. The last part of the climb looks worse than it is, if I can do it then anyone can, lots of locals around to help. The views from the top are breath taking, I could have stayed there for ages. Wear good shoes and enjoy it
title: A Highlight of my Trip

body: We wanted to visit the pingurala rock instead of Sigeriya because of the crowd. As I the entrance table located on in the temple on the path to the start of climb, I was informed that my wife who is in hijab have to take off her hijab not only to cross the temple but have to keep it off during climb. She was willing to do while crossing the temple lawn but could not understand why she need to keep it off during climb. In brief we rejected to climb
title: Caution for Muslim women in Hijab

body: This is an awesome trip. Recommend either in the morning for sunrise but that will be a very early start or afternoon for the sunset. It is quite a climb up to the top including scrambling over lots of rocks and steep steps. You definitely need some level of fitness, the views are just awesome and of course just a few local dogs at the top!
title: amazing trip

body: We weren´t really lucky about weather at this one, after pretty adventurous climb before Sunrise we watched Lion´s Rock´s impressive shape starting to appear in a mist which felt really mysterious. Anyway we didn´t see much from view over landscapes which I believe must be gorgeous while Sun coming up. There were just few people with us and entrance was low (500lkr) so definitely worth it, but I recommend to visit Lion´s Rock especially. No water to buy anywhere nearby, take yours with you, after climb that is not that comfy as Sigiriya you might need it (at some points you have to climb steep parts that are missing proper stairs and so on). Hiking shoes recommended.
title: Grand view over Lion´s Rock

body: Having just been to the top of Sigiriya Rock as this is only about 1.5 kilometers away if you have energy don't miss out on Pidurangala Cave and Rock Temple. Also the cost was only 500 rupees which was nothing. The first part of the climb is up steps but the last section after the buddha is a real scramble which will test you as there are no steps. There is a great view of Sigiriya from the top, so well worth the climb, which is the main attraction. The whole trip took me an hour.
title: The last bit of the climb is a bit tricky but worth it

body: It was really nice day, stunning view. Entrance fee was 500 rupees per person! Beautiful view to Lion Rock! Recommend! It takes about 30 minutes to climb up
title: Great

body: After a moderate climb (exept the end is a bit heavier) we arrived on top and had a stunning view of the area. One big plus is that you paying a normal price (500rps) Hopefully the government wil keep it like that but the system is money-hungry, corruption is an expensive hobby ;-)
title: Not the high prices than normally in Sri Lanka highlights

body: One of the scenic places to visit. We went on the hike to Pidurangala Jan 2019 in an afternoon. Climb was difficult but enjoyable .On the summit it’s a breathtaking view 360degree including the famous Sigiriya Rock. Sunset was awesome and the wind on the top will keep you relaxed. Must visit again...!Dr Piyal Kurukulasooriya
title: Pidurangala visit

body: The view from Lion Rock is amazing. With my husband we went to the sunrise, you can go by your self or you can hire a tour, that they can help you with some light during the climbing
title: A Must

body: Views of Lion Rock are incredible. A lot more fun to climb than Lion Rock and significantly cheaper.
title: Exceptional views
Hard at the end
body: Great view and a nice walk. But at the end you had to climb to get to the top which we didn't mind but some older or unfit people had to turn around. We went there by bicycle from lal homestay which was just great.

title: Beautiful vantage point
body: Highly recommended to set off early morning so you can be at the top for sunrise. Plan extra early as the trail is narrow at the top and you could get trapped behind a group less capable of getting up the final boulders. We were very disappointed to leave the resort later than planned. Even though we raced up the trail, when we got to the top the final accent was blocked by a group of tourists trying to lift all their camera equipment, backpacks and seniors up the slippery gigantic boulders. Once on top the view (despite missing the sunrise) was spectacular. We brought food for the dogs.

title: Pidurangala Rock
body: Best time to visit this place is early morning. You may start at 5 am in morning so reach by 6 Am to watch sunrise.Take torch and wear proper shoes..its very tough as some part there are no steps but you have to climb rock. Entry Fee is 500 Sri Lankan Money.take water along with you.

title: Chaotic, fun-filled adventure
body: We climbed the Pidurangala rock during a visit to Sigiriya. We were amazed by the lack of signage to this relatively unkbown and undeveloped site. The rock has to be accessed through a buddhist temple site (Pidurangala Raja Maha Viharaya) and all have to adhere to a strict dress code and attire while passing the temple site. This includes removing shoes and footwear and modest dresses for women covering legs, which may not suit rock climbing. Luckily, the temple offers drapes free of charge for women at the entrance. The first half of the climb has narrow steps but the latter half has no such help such as guard rails and can be challenging even for physically fit people. Certain sections of the climb involves scaling under rocks and climbing steep-angled rocks, which require a second person to help out from the other end. So stick to your group. We climbed the rock on a full moon day (a buddhist holiday) and it was very crowded and took longer to climb. Nevertheless, we, including our teenage kids enjoyed the challenge of climbing the rock and the amazing scenary at the top of the rock. So be prepared for these little minor incoveniences but you will enjoy the climb. I thoroughly recommend it for physically fit and agile people but not for the elderly and younger children.

title: Chaotic and crowded route up but worth it for the view
body: I did this straight after climbing Sigiriya, to give me an alternative perspective on the rock. The path up to Pidarangala climbs up past a small rock temple, so you'll have to pay the 500LKR fee and take your shoes off (and make sure your dress is appropriate though this didn't seem to be rigorously enforced!) before you can get to the start of the hike. Again, like most famous Sri Lankan hikes, it seems to be mostly steps, at least for the first 1-1.5km anyway. Then it becomes much more rocky and technical - don't get me wrong, you don't need climbing skills, but they'd help if you want to avoid the worst of the crowds getting caught in the bottlenecks up through here! And trust me, you'll encounter these from the first of the boulders to the top of the hike! Anywhere else in the world you'll be told to dress appropriately for technical hiking with a decent pair of boots on. Not here, so the way is inevitably blocked by people who should know better, wearing flip flops (at best!), and frequently passing young children up and down. There are points where you could easily be stopped from moving for maybe an hour - this is where climbing skills help, you can try and find an alternative route! The view from the top is worth it though, you won't find a better view of Sigiriya really, and if (unlike me) you get up there on a sunny day (or for sunset) your pics should be pretty epic! The route down is a reciprocal hence the mad bottlenecks - I tried to avoid this by taking a short-cut. I don't recommend this - I got lost in the forest and went well out of my way to get back!
